summary.en: The sisters Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị led the Lạc lords of the Red River delta in revolt against the Han governor of Jiaozhi and ruled for about three years from Mê Linh, until the Han general Ma Yuan crushed the rising in 43.
summary.zh: 征侧、征贰姐妹率领红河三角洲的雒将起兵反抗东汉交趾太守，以麊泠为中心自立约三年，43年被东汉将领马援镇压。

sources.title: Hou Hanshu (Book of the Later Han), "Biography of Ma Yuan" and "Treatise on the Southern Man"
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Trưng sisters' rebellion

story.en:
In 40 CE the Han governor of Jiaozhi, Su Ding, is said to have executed Thi Sách, a Lạc lord and husband of Trưng Trắc. Trắc and her sister Nhị raised the Lạc lords of the Red River delta in revolt; the Han histories record that sixty-five towns joined them and that the governor fled. Trắc was proclaimed queen at Mê Linh.

The Han court sent its veteran general Ma Yuan, who marched south with some 20,000 men and a fleet in 42. The sisters' forces were defeated at Lãng Bạc in 43. Chinese sources say Ma Yuan captured and beheaded them; Vietnamese tradition says they drowned themselves in the Hát river rather than surrender.

Ma Yuan then reorganised the delta under direct Han administration and is credited with erecting bronze pillars marking the frontier. The sisters became the first heroes of Vietnamese resistance to the north, honoured with temples, a national holiday and streets in every city.
story.zh:
据载，公元40年东汉交趾太守苏定处死了雒将诗索，即征侧的丈夫。征侧与妹妹征贰发动红河三角洲的雒将起兵；《后汉书》记载有六十五城响应，太守出逃。征侧在麊泠被拥立为王。

汉廷派老将马援于42年率约两万人和水军南下。43年，二征的军队在浪泊战败。中国史书称马援擒获并斩杀二人，越南传说则称她们宁死不降，投喝江自尽。

马援随后将三角洲纳入汉朝直接管辖，相传还立铜柱为界。二征姐妹成为越南反抗北方的第一代英雄，各地建有祠庙，设有纪念日，每座城市都有以她们命名的街道。

name.en: Kedukan Bukit inscription: rise of Srivijaya
name.zh: 格杜干武吉碑：室利佛逝兴起

summary.en: This Old Malay inscription found at Palembang records a sacred expedition by Dapunta Hyang with an army of some 20,000 in 683, commonly read as the founding of the Srivijaya polity that soon dominated the Strait of Malacca.
summary.zh: 在巨港发现的这块古马来语碑铭，记载了683年达本达·希扬率两万大军进行的神圣远征，通常被解读为室利佛逝政权的建立；此后不久它便称霸马六甲海峡。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
O. W. Wolters, Early Indonesian Commerce: A Study of the Origins of Śrīvijaya (Cornell University Press, 1967)
Wikipedia: Kedukan Bukit inscription

note: Interpretation of the expedition as a "founding" is debated; the inscription is dated Śaka 605 (683 CE).

summary.en: The Shailendra dynasty of central Java raised Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist monument: a stepped mandala of nine platforms with over 2,600 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues, built around 780–830.
summary.zh: 中爪哇的夏连特拉王朝建造了世界上最大的佛教建筑婆罗浮屠：一座九层阶梯式曼荼罗，拥有两千六百多块浮雕和五百零四尊佛像，约建于780至830年间。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Borobudur
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Borobudur Temple Compounds
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Borobudur

note: No foundation inscription survives; construction is dated by style and epigraphy to c. 780–830.

story.en:
Borobudur was built by the Shailendra kings of Central Java over perhaps fifty years around 800, on a hill above the Kedu plain. It is not a temple with an interior but a stepped mountain of some 55,000 cubic metres of andesite: pilgrims climb clockwise through square galleries carved with the life of the Buddha and the pilgrimage of Sudhana, up to three round terraces where 72 perforated stupas each enclose a seated Buddha.

The kingdom's centre moved to East Java in the 10th century and the monument was gradually covered by ash and jungle, though it was never wholly forgotten by local villagers. In 1814 Stamford Raffles, then governing Java, sent the engineer H. C. Cornelius to clear it.

The Dutch restored it in 1907–1911 under Theodoor van Erp, and UNESCO and Indonesia dismantled and rebuilt the lower terraces in 1975–1982 to install drainage. It became a World Heritage site in 1991 and is again a place of Vesak pilgrimage.
story.zh:
婆罗浮屠由中爪哇的夏连特拉王朝在公元800年前后历时约五十年建成，坐落在格都平原上方的山丘上。它并不是一座有内部空间的神庙，而是一座用约五万五千立方米安山岩堆砌的阶梯形“圣山”：朝圣者顺时针沿方形回廊攀登，回廊浮雕讲述佛陀生平和善财童子参访的故事，顶部是三层圆台，72座镂空小塔中各有一尊坐佛。

10世纪王国中心东移，这座建筑逐渐被火山灰和丛林覆盖，不过当地村民从未完全遗忘它。1814年，统治爪哇的莱佛士派工程师科内利乌斯前去清理。

荷兰人于1907—1911年在范埃尔普主持下进行修复；1975—1982年联合国教科文组织与印尼拆解并重建了下层平台，加装排水系统。1991年它列入世界遗产，如今再次成为卫塞节朝圣之地。

summary.en: The Shivagrha inscription of 856 records the completion of a great Shiva temple, identified with Prambanan, by the Sanjaya-line ruler of Mataram. Its soaring towers to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma are Java's largest Hindu monument.
summary.zh: 856年的湿婆屋碑铭记载了马打兰古国桑贾亚系君主建成一座宏伟的湿婆神庙，即普兰巴南。其供奉湿婆、毗湿奴与梵天的高塔是爪哇最大的印度教建筑群。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Prambanan
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Prambanan Temple Compounds
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Prambanan

note: Wikidata gives c. 850; 856 is the date of the Shivagrha inscription usually associated with the complex.

summary.en: Ngô Quyền planted iron-tipped stakes in the bed of the Bạch Đằng River and lured a Southern Han fleet over them at high tide; as the tide fell the ships were impaled and destroyed. The victory ended a millennium of Chinese rule in northern Vietnam.
summary.zh: 吴权在白藤江河床中埋下包铁木桩，趁涨潮引诱南汉舰队驶入，退潮时敌船触桩搁浅而被歼灭。此役结束了中国对越南北部近千年的统治。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Wikipedia: Battle of Bạch Đằng (938)

story.en:
In 937 the Vietnamese governor Dương Đình Nghệ was murdered by his subordinate Kiều Công Tiễn, who asked the Southern Han kingdom in Guangzhou for help. Đình Nghệ's son-in-law Ngô Quyền marched on the capital, killed the usurper and prepared to meet the Han fleet commanded by the crown prince Liu Hongcao.

According to the Vietnamese annals, he had his men drive iron-tipped wooden stakes into the bed of the Bạch Đằng estuary, hidden at high tide. Small boats lured the Han warships upriver over the stakes; when the tide went out the heavy ships were caught, holed and destroyed, and Liu Hongcao was killed.

In 939 Ngô Quyền proclaimed himself king at Cổ Loa, the ancient capital, ending about a thousand years of Chinese rule. The stake tactic was used again at the same river in 981 and, most famously, against the Mongols in 1288.
story.zh:
937年，越南静海军节度使杨廷艺被部将矫公羡杀害，矫公羡向广州的南汉求援。杨廷艺的女婿吴权举兵攻入大罗，杀死篡位者，并准备迎战南汉太子刘弘操率领的舰队。

据越南史书记载，他命部下在白藤江口的河床上打下包铁尖头的木桩，涨潮时木桩隐没水下。吴权以小船诱敌，引南汉战船越过木桩上溯；退潮后，沉重的战船被木桩卡住、刺穿而覆没，刘弘操战死。

939年吴权在古都古螺称王，结束了约一千年的北属时期。这一木桩战术在981年和1288年又两度用于白藤江，后者对蒙古军一役最为著名。

name.en: Lý Thái Tổ moves the capital to Thăng Long

summary.en: In his Edict on the Transfer of the Capital, Lý Thái Tổ moved the court from Hoa Lư to the site of the old Tang citadel of Đại La, renaming it Thăng Long ("Ascending Dragon"), the future Hanoi.
summary.zh: 李太祖颁布《迁都诏》，将朝廷从华闾迁至唐代大罗城旧址，并改名升龙（意为“腾飞之龙”），即后来的河内。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long – Hanoi
Wikipedia: Edict on the Transfer of the Capital

summary.en: King Suryavarman II built Angkor Wat as a temple to Vishnu and probably his own funerary monument. Its five lotus towers, moat and kilometre-long bas-reliefs make it the largest religious monument in the world.
summary.zh: 苏利耶跋摩二世修建吴哥窟，供奉毗湿奴，很可能也是其陵庙。五座莲花状宝塔、护城河与绵延近一公里的浮雕回廊，使其成为世界上最大的宗教建筑。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Angkor Wat
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Angkor Wat

note: Wikidata gives an inception of 1200; scholarly consensus places construction in the reign of Suryavarman II (1113–c. 1150).

story.en:
Suryavarman II seized the Khmer throne in 1113 after defeating a rival, and spent much of his reign at war with Đại Việt and Champa. At home he built the largest temple of all. Angkor Wat faces west, the direction associated with death, and was dedicated to Vishnu rather than Shiva; most scholars think it was meant as his mausoleum as well as a state temple.

Its plan is a model of the Hindu cosmos: a moat for the ocean, galleries for mountain ranges and five towers for the peaks of Mount Meru. The outer gallery carries some 800 metres of bas-reliefs, among them the Churning of the Ocean of Milk and a procession of Suryavarman's army, in which the king himself sits under fifteen parasols.

Unlike most of Angkor, the temple was never abandoned. It became a Theravada Buddhist monastery, Japanese pilgrims sketched it in the 17th century, and Henri Mouhot's account of 1860 made it famous in Europe. Its silhouette has been on every Cambodian flag since independence.
story.zh:
苏利耶跋摩二世于1113年击败对手夺取高棉王位，在位期间大多与大越和占城交战。在国内，他建造了最宏大的神庙。吴哥窟坐东朝西，西方与死亡相联系；神庙供奉的是毗湿奴而非湿婆，多数学者认为它既是国家神庙，也是国王的陵寝。

其布局是印度教宇宙的缩影：护城河象征大海，回廊象征山脉，五座宝塔象征须弥山诸峰。外回廊有约800米长的浮雕，其中有“搅拌乳海”，以及苏利耶跋摩大军的行进场面，国王本人端坐在十五顶华盖之下。

与吴哥大部分建筑不同，这座神庙从未被废弃。它后来成为上座部佛教寺院，17世纪有日本朝圣者为它绘图，1860年亨利·穆奥的游记使它在欧洲声名大噪。独立以来，柬埔寨的每一面国旗上都有它的剪影。

summary.en: At the centre of his new walled city of Angkor Thom, Jayavarman VII raised the Buddhist Bayon, famous for its towers carved with serene giant faces and reliefs of daily life and wars with Champa.
summary.zh: 阇耶跋摩七世在新建的吴哥城中心修建佛教寺庙巴戎寺，以刻有巨大安详面孔的佛塔群和描绘日常生活及与占婆战争的浮雕而闻名。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: the Bayon
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Bayon

note: Built over several phases in the late 12th and early 13th centuries; 1190 is an approximate date.

name.en: Mongol invasions of Đại Việt and Champa

summary.en: Three Mongol–Yuan invasions (1258, 1285, 1287–88) took Thăng Long but were each driven out by the Trần dynasty under Trần Hưng Đạo, who used scorched-earth tactics and guerrilla warfare before the decisive river battle at Bạch Đằng.
summary.zh: 蒙古—元朝先后三次（1258年、1285年、1287—1288年）入侵，虽曾攻占升龙，但都被陈朝击退。陈兴道采取坚壁清野与游击战术，最终在白藤江决战中获胜。

label.zh: 兀良合台自大理（云南）出兵

label.en: Thăng Long taken, then retaken by Trần forces
label.zh: 升龙失守后被陈军收复

label.en: Yuan fleet destroyed at Bạch Đằng
label.zh: 元军舰队覆灭于白藤江

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Annan zhuan" and "Zhaowa zhuan"
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasions of Vietnam

story.en:
Đại Việt faced the Mongols three times. In 1258 a Mongol army coming down from Yunnan took Thăng Long but, ravaged by heat and disease, soon withdrew. After Kublai founded the Yuan dynasty, his demands for submission grew, and in 1285 his son Toghan invaded with a huge army while another force under Sogetu attacked from Champa in the south.

The Trần court abandoned the capital. Before the campaign, according to the annals, the retired emperor Trần Thánh Tông summoned village elders to the Diên Hồng conference and asked whether to fight or yield, and they answered with one voice: fight. Trần Hưng Đạo, the commander, emptied the countryside of food, harassed the Yuan columns and struck when they were exhausted; Sogetu was killed and Toghan fled.

The third invasion, in 1287–88, again took Thăng Long and again starved when its supply fleet was sunk at Vân Đồn. Retreating, the Yuan navy was destroyed at Bạch Đằng. The Trần then sent tribute to Kublai, who planned a fourth invasion that his death in 1294 cancelled.
story.zh:
大越三次抗击蒙古。1258年，蒙古军从云南南下攻占升龙，但不堪酷暑和疫病，很快撤退。忽必烈建立元朝后，要求大越臣服的压力日增，1285年其子脱欢率大军入侵，另一路由唆都从南方的占城进攻。

陈朝王廷放弃了都城。据史书记载，战前太上皇陈圣宗召集各地父老举行“延洪会议”，问战还是降，众人齐声回答：战。统帅陈兴道坚壁清野，袭扰元军各路，待其疲惫时出击；唆都战死，脱欢逃回。

1287—1288年的第三次入侵再度攻占升龙，但其运粮船队在云屯被击沉，元军再次陷入饥困。撤退途中，元朝水军在白藤江全军覆没。此后陈朝向忽必烈朝贡；忽必烈曾计划第四次入侵，因1294年去世而作罢。

summary.en: Repeating Ngô Quyền's tactic, Trần Hưng Đạo staked the Bạch Đằng River and trapped the withdrawing Yuan fleet under Omar at low tide, destroying it and ending the third Mongol invasion.
summary.zh: 陈兴道效仿吴权的战法，在白藤江中埋设木桩，趁退潮困住撤退中的元朝乌马儿舰队并将其歼灭，结束了元朝第三次入侵。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Annan zhuan" and "Zhaowa zhuan"
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Battle of Bạch Đằng (1288)

story.en:
By the spring of 1288 the third Yuan invasion of Đại Việt had failed: its grain fleet had been destroyed at Vân Đồn, and the army in Thăng Long was starving. Prince Toghan decided to withdraw by land, while the fleet under Omar sailed for the sea down the Bạch Đằng river.

Trần Hưng Đạo knew the river and its history. Like Ngô Quyền 350 years earlier, he had stakes driven into the riverbed at the estuary and hid his boats in the side channels. On 9 April 1288 Vietnamese boats engaged the Yuan fleet at high tide and drew it on; as the tide fell, the ships ran onto the stakes. Hundreds were sunk or captured, and Omar was taken prisoner.

The victory ended the Mongol threat to Đại Việt. Some of the original stakes have been found in the fields that now cover the old riverbed near Quảng Ninh, and the battle remains the most celebrated in Vietnamese history.
story.zh:
到1288年春，元朝第三次入侵大越已告失败：运粮船队在云屯被毁，驻升龙的元军陷入饥荒。脱欢决定从陆路撤退，乌马儿则率水军沿白藤江出海。

陈兴道熟知这条河及其历史。他效法350年前的吴权，命人在江口河床打下木桩，把船只藏在支流中。1288年4月9日涨潮时，越军船只与元军舰队交战并诱其前行；潮水退落，元船纷纷撞上木桩。数百艘战船被击沉或俘获，乌马儿被生擒。

这场胜利解除了蒙古对大越的威胁。在广宁附近覆盖旧河床的田野中，已发掘出部分当年的木桩。此役至今仍是越南历史上最受颂扬的战役。

summary.en: Kublai Khan sent a fleet to punish King Kertanegara of Singhasari for mutilating his envoy. Raden Wijaya allied with the Yuan to defeat the usurper Jayakatwang, then turned on and expelled them, founding Majapahit.
summary.zh: 忽必烈派遣舰队惩罚曾黥面元使的新柯沙里国王格尔达纳卡拉。罗登·威查耶先与元军联手击败篡位者查耶卡旺，随后反戈驱逐元军，建立了满者伯夷。

sources.title: Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Annan zhuan" and "Zhaowa zhuan"
Pararaton (Book of Kings, 15th–16th c.)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasion of Java

summary.en: Lê Lợi raised a rebellion against Ming occupation at Lam Sơn in Thanh Hóa. After a decade of guerrilla war and the destruction of a Ming relief army at Chi Lăng in 1427, the Ming withdrew and Lê Lợi founded the Later Lê dynasty.
summary.zh: 黎利在清化蓝山起兵反抗明朝统治。经过十年游击战，并于1427年在支棱歼灭明朝援军后，明军撤离，黎利建立后黎朝。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Lam Sơn uprising

summary.en: An Ayutthayan army besieged and took the Khmer capital. The Khmer court soon moved south toward the Phnom Penh area, closing the Angkorian era.
summary.zh: 阿瑜陀耶军队围攻并攻陷高棉都城。高棉王廷随后南迁至金边一带，吴哥时代就此结束。

sources.title: David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Royal Chronicles of Ayutthaya, trans. Richard D. Cushman (Siam Society, 2000)
Wikipedia: Fall of Angkor

note: The 1431 date comes from later chronicles; historians see Angkor's decline as gradual and the date as conventional.

summary.en: The fugitive Palembang prince Parameswara settled at Malacca around 1400. With Ming recognition and its command of the strait, the port grew into the greatest entrepôt of Southeast Asia and a centre for the spread of Islam.
summary.zh: 流亡的巨港王子拜里米苏拉约在1400年定居马六甲。凭借明朝的册封和对海峡的控制，这座港口发展为东南亚最大的转口贸易中心，也是伊斯兰教传播的中心。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sultanate of Malacca
Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals), trans. C. C. Brown (1952)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca Sultanate

note: Founding dates between c. 1396 and 1402 are proposed.

story.en:
According to the Malay Annals, Parameswara was a prince of Palembang descended from Srivijaya's kings who fled after a failed bid for independence from Majapahit, ruled Temasek (Singapore) for a time and fled again, northwards. Resting by a river, he saw a mouse-deer kick one of his hunting dogs into the water, took it as an omen and founded a town there, naming it after the melaka tree he was sitting under.

The new port lay at the narrowest part of the strait, where the monsoons met. Parameswara placed it under the protection of the Ming emperor; Zheng He's fleets used it as a depot, and in 1411 Parameswara sailed to Nanjing with his wife and 540 followers to pay homage in person.

Malacca's rulers adopted Islam in the early 15th century and attracted Gujarati, Tamil, Javanese and Chinese merchants. The Portuguese apothecary Tomé Pires wrote that whoever was lord of Malacca had his hand on the throat of Venice. Its court language and customs became the model of Malay culture.
story.zh:
据《马来纪年》记载，拜里米苏拉是室利佛逝王族后裔、巨港的王子，因试图摆脱满者伯夷失败而出逃，曾一度统治淡马锡（新加坡），后又北逃。他在河边歇息时，看到一只鼠鹿把他的猎犬踢进水里，认为是吉兆，便在此建城，以他身旁的马六甲树为名。

新港位于海峡最狭窄处，正是季风交汇之地。拜里米苏拉将其置于明朝皇帝的保护之下；郑和船队以此为补给站，1411年拜里米苏拉还携妻子和随从540人亲赴南京朝贡。

15世纪初，马六甲统治者皈依伊斯兰教，吸引了古吉拉特、泰米尔、爪哇和中国商人。葡萄牙药剂师托梅·皮雷斯写道，谁掌握了马六甲，谁就扼住了威尼斯的咽喉。马六甲的宫廷语言和习俗成为马来文化的典范。

summary.en: Afonso de Albuquerque's fleet stormed Malacca after weeks of fighting, driving out Sultan Mahmud Shah. Portugal gained a key base on the spice route, while Muslim traders dispersed to rival ports such as Aceh, Johor and Banten.
summary.zh: 阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克的舰队经数周激战攻占马六甲，苏丹马哈茂德沙出逃。葡萄牙由此获得香料航线上的关键据点，穆斯林商人则分散到亚齐、柔佛、万丹等竞争港口。

sources.title: Brás de Albuquerque, Commentaries of the Great Afonso Dalboquerque (1557; Hakluyt Society trans. 1875–84)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Capture of Malacca (1511)

story.en:
In 1509 a Portuguese trading squadron at Malacca was attacked and some of its men taken prisoner, on the advice, the Portuguese believed, of Muslim merchants. Two years later Afonso de Albuquerque, governor of Portuguese India, arrived with about eighteen ships and a thousand or so Portuguese and Indian soldiers to demand their release and the right to build a fort.

Sultan Mahmud Shah refused. On 25 July 1511 Albuquerque attacked the bridge that joined the two halves of the town across the river; a second assault in August, with a tall junk used as a floating siege tower, carried the bridge and the town. After days of street fighting and sack, the sultan fled inland and his son later founded the Johor sultanate.

Albuquerque built the fortress of A Famosa from the stones of mosques and royal tombs. But the trading network Malacca had commanded dispersed: Muslim merchants moved to Aceh, Johor, Brunei and Banten, and Portuguese Malacca never matched the city it had conquered.
story.zh:
1509年，一支在马六甲贸易的葡萄牙船队遭到攻击，部分人员被扣押，葡萄牙人认为这是穆斯林商人唆使所致。两年后，葡属印度总督阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克率约十八艘船和一千余名葡萄牙及印度士兵到来，要求释放俘虏并准许建造堡垒。

马哈茂德·沙苏丹予以拒绝。1511年7月25日，阿尔布克尔克进攻连接河两岸城区的桥梁；8月发动第二次进攻时，他把一艘高大的帆船当作浮动攻城塔，夺下了桥梁和城市。经过数日巷战和劫掠，苏丹逃往内地，其子后来建立了柔佛苏丹国。

阿尔布克尔克用清真寺和王陵的石块建造了“法摩沙”堡垒。然而马六甲原先掌控的贸易网络随之星散：穆斯林商人转往亚齐、柔佛、文莱和万丹，葡属马六甲始终未能重现被征服前的繁荣。

summary.en: Ferdinand Magellan, seeking to force the chief Lapulapu to submit to his Christian ally Rajah Humabon of Cebu, landed on Mactan with about 50 men and was killed. The expedition sailed on and completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.
summary.zh: 麦哲伦为迫使酋长拉普拉普臣服于已受洗的宿务王胡马邦，率约五十人登陆麦克坦岛，结果战死。船队继续航行，并于1522年完成首次环球航行。

label.en: Exits the Strait of Magellan into the Pacific (Nov 1520)
label.zh: 驶出麦哲伦海峡进入太平洋（1520年11月）
利马萨瓦岛：首次弥撒（3月31日）

sources.title: Antonio Pigafetta, Relazione del primo viaggio intorno al mondo (c. 1524), trans. R. A. Skelton (1969)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ferdinand Magellan
Wikipedia: Battle of Mactan

note: QID Q2091449 is the correct item, but its English label on Wikidata is currently vandalised ("Battle of Six Seven"); this record does not use the Wikidata label, and the label should be reverted on Wikidata.

story.en:
Ferdinand Magellan reached the Philippines in March 1521, the first Europeans to cross the Pacific. At Cebu its ruler, Rajah Humabon, accepted baptism with hundreds of his people and received an image of the Christ Child. Magellan then demanded that the other chiefs of the area submit to Humabon and to Spain. Lapulapu, a chief on the small island of Mactan, refused.

On 27 April Magellan crossed to Mactan with about fifty men, telling Humabon's warriors to stay in their boats and watch. Because of the reef the ships could not come close enough for their guns to help. According to Antonio Pigafetta, who was wounded beside him, the Spaniards waded ashore against more than a thousand warriors, were driven back to the water and Magellan, struck in the leg and then by many spears, was killed.

Humabon soon turned on the survivors and killed many of them at a banquet. The remnants sailed on, and one ship under Juan Sebastián Elcano returned to Spain in 1522. Lapulapu is honoured in the Philippines as the first to resist European colonisation.
story.zh:
1521年3月，斐迪南·麦哲伦抵达菲律宾，成为最早横渡太平洋的欧洲人。宿务统治者拉者胡马邦与数百名臣民接受洗礼，并获赠一尊圣婴像。麦哲伦随后要求周边各首领臣服于胡马邦和西班牙，麦克坦小岛上的首领拉普拉普拒不从命。

4月27日，麦哲伦带着约五十人渡海到麦克坦，让胡马邦的战士留在船上观战。由于珊瑚礁阻隔，大船无法靠近以火炮支援。据在他身旁负伤的安东尼奥·皮加费塔记述，西班牙人涉水上岸，面对一千多名战士，被逼退到水中；麦哲伦腿部中箭，又被许多长矛刺中，最终阵亡。

胡马邦不久便反目，在宴会上杀死了许多幸存者。残部继续航行，胡安·塞巴斯蒂安·埃尔卡诺率一艘船于1522年回到西班牙。拉普拉普在菲律宾被尊为第一位反抗欧洲殖民的英雄。

summary.en: After defeating Rajah Sulayman's Maynila, Miguel López de Legazpi proclaimed the Spanish city of Manila, later walled as Intramuros. It became the capital of the Spanish Philippines and the Asian terminus of the Manila galleons to Acapulco.
summary.zh: 米格尔·洛佩斯·德·黎牙实比击败苏莱曼王统治的马尼拉后，宣布建立西班牙马尼拉城，后筑城墙成为王城区（Intramuros）。这里成为西属菲律宾首府和通往阿卡普尔科的马尼拉大帆船贸易的亚洲终点。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Intramuros
Emma H. Blair & James A. Robertson (eds.), The Philippine Islands, 1493–1898, Vol. 3 (1903)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Intramuros

story.en:
After founding the first Spanish town at Cebu in 1565, Miguel López de Legazpi heard of a wealthy Muslim port on Luzon, Maynila, ruled by Rajah Sulayman and allied with Brunei. In 1570 his grandson Juan de Salcedo and Martín de Goiti attacked it and burned the stockade; the next year Legazpi arrived in force and, after negotiations with Sulayman and his kinsmen broke down, defeated them.

On 24 June 1571 Legazpi proclaimed Manila a Spanish city and capital of the islands. It was walled in stone in the 1590s as Intramuros, with churches, convents and the governor's palace inside. Outside the walls lay the Parián, where thousands of Chinese merchants and artisans lived; they were indispensable to the city and repeatedly massacred, in 1603 and 1639.

Manila's fortune came from the galleon trade with Acapulco, which brought Mexican silver in exchange for Chinese goods. It remained Spain's Asian capital until 1898.
story.zh:
1565年在宿务建立西班牙的第一个城镇后，米格尔·洛佩斯·德黎牙实比得知吕宋岛有一个富庶的穆斯林港口马尼拉，由拉者苏莱曼统治，并与文莱结盟。1570年，他的孙子胡安·德萨尔塞多和马丁·德戈伊蒂进攻该地，烧毁了木寨；次年黎牙实比亲率大军前来，与苏莱曼及其族人谈判破裂后将其击败。

1571年6月24日，黎牙实比宣布马尼拉为西班牙城市和群岛首府。16世纪90年代筑起石墙，称“王城”（Intramuros），城内有教堂、修道院和总督府。城外的“八连”住着数以千计的华人商人和工匠，他们是城市不可或缺的力量，却在1603年和1639年一再遭到屠杀。

马尼拉的财富来自与阿卡普尔科的大帆船贸易，以墨西哥白银换取中国货物。直到1898年它一直是西班牙在亚洲的首府。

summary.en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) destroyed the town of Jayakarta and built Batavia on its ruins. It became the VOC's Asian headquarters and later the capital of the Dutch East Indies.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司的扬·彼得生·库恩摧毁查雅加达城，并在废墟上兴建巴达维亚。这里成为荷兰东印度公司的亚洲总部，后来成为荷属东印度首府。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Batavia, Dutch East Indies

story.en:
In 1618 Jayakarta, a pepper port under the Sultan of Banten, was crowded with rival Europeans. The English, allied with the local prince, besieged the small Dutch fort there, and Jan Pieterszoon Coen, the VOC's new governor-general, sailed to the Moluccas to fetch reinforcements. The garrison held out, and in May 1619 Coen returned, stormed Jayakarta, burned it to the ground and drove out its people.

On the ruins he built a walled Dutch town, Batavia, laid out with canals like Amsterdam, which he wanted to call New Hoorn after his home town; the directors chose the Latin name of the ancient Dutch tribe instead. To populate it Coen brought in Chinese settlers, slaves from Bali, Bengal and South India, and Mardijkers, free Christian Asians.

Batavia became the headquarters of the VOC's Asian network and, after 1800, of the Dutch East Indies. Its low, canal-ridden site bred malaria, earning it the name "graveyard of the Dutch". As Jakarta it became the capital of independent Indonesia.
story.zh:
1618年，万丹苏丹治下的胡椒港雅加特拉挤满了互相竞争的欧洲人。英国人与当地王公结盟，围攻那里的荷兰小堡垒，荷兰东印度公司新任总督扬·彼得生·库恩航往马鲁古搬取援兵。守军坚持了下来，1619年5月库恩返回，攻占雅加特拉，将其夷为平地，驱逐了当地居民。

他在废墟上建起一座仿照阿姆斯特丹、运河纵横的荷兰城市巴达维亚。库恩原想以家乡之名称之为“新霍伦”，董事会却选用了古代荷兰部落的拉丁名。为充实人口，库恩引进华人移民，从巴厘、孟加拉和南印度输入奴隶，还招来信奉基督教的自由亚洲人“马尔代克人”。

巴达维亚成为荷兰东印度公司亚洲网络的总部，1800年后又成为荷属东印度的首府。低洼多渠的地势滋生疟疾，使它得了“荷兰人的坟场”之名。改称雅加达后，它成为独立的印度尼西亚首都。

name.en: Burmese–Siamese War and fall of Ayutthaya
name.zh: 缅暹战争与阿瑜陀耶陷落

summary.en: Konbaung Burma under Hsinbyushin invaded Siam on two fronts and, after a 14-month siege, sacked and burned Ayutthaya in April 1767, ending the 417-year-old kingdom. Taksin soon regrouped the Siamese at Thonburi.
summary.zh: 贡榜王朝孟驳王分两路入侵暹罗，经十四个月围城，于1767年4月攻陷并焚毁阿瑜陀耶，延续四百余年的王国就此灭亡。不久郑信在吞武里重整暹罗力量。

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
Wikipedia: Burmese–Siamese War (1765–1767)

story.en:
King Hsinbyushin of Burma, son of Alaungpaya, sent two armies into Siam in 1765, one from Chiang Mai in the north and one from Tavoy in the west. They converged on Ayutthaya in early 1766 and settled in for a long siege, sitting out the rainy season on high ground while the floods surrounded the island city.

Ayutthaya was strong but badly led; the chronicles blame King Ekkathat and quarrelling nobles. Famine and fire weakened the city, and offers to surrender as a vassal were refused. On 7 April 1767 the Burmese breached the walls. The city was looted and burned, temples stripped of their gold, and tens of thousands of people, including the royal family, were marched away to Burma. Ekkathat died, possibly of starvation, in hiding.

The Burmese had to withdraw quickly to meet a Qing invasion in the north. Within months Taksin, a provincial governor who had escaped before the fall, rebuilt Siamese power from the east coast, and the capital moved downriver to Thonburi and then Bangkok. Ayutthaya's ruins are now a World Heritage site.
story.zh:
雍籍牙之子、缅王孟驳于1765年派两路大军入侵暹罗，一路从北方的清迈，一路从西边的土瓦。两军于1766年初会师阿瑜陀耶城下，展开长期围困，雨季时驻扎在高地上，任由洪水环绕这座岛城。

阿瑜陀耶城防坚固，但指挥无能；史书归咎于厄伽陀王和互相倾轧的贵族。饥荒和火灾削弱了城市，暹罗提出以藩属身份投降也遭拒绝。1767年4月7日，缅军攻破城墙。城市遭洗劫焚烧，寺庙的黄金被剥光，包括王室在内的数万人被押往缅甸。厄伽陀王藏匿时身亡，可能是饿死的。

缅军不得不迅速撤兵，以应对北方清军的入侵。数月之内，城破前突围而出的府尹郑信在东海岸重建暹罗力量，都城随后南迁到吞武里，再迁至曼谷。阿瑜陀耶遗址如今是世界遗产。

summary.en: King Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, moved the capital across the Chao Phraya from Thonburi to Rattanakosin Island, setting the city pillar on 21 April 1782 and building the Grand Palace.
summary.zh: 却克里王朝开国君主拉玛一世将都城从吞武里迁至湄南河对岸的拉达那哥欣岛，于1782年4月21日立城柱，并修建大皇宫。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Rattanakosin Island

summary.en: Nguyễn Huệ of the Tây Sơn, newly proclaimed Emperor Quang Trung, made a lightning march north during Tết and routed the Qing army that had occupied Thăng Long to restore the Lê, ending Qing intervention.
summary.zh: 西山朝阮惠刚称帝号光中，便于春节期间率军急行北上，击溃为扶持黎朝而占据升龙的清军，结束了清朝的干预。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Battle of Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa

note: Wikidata gives 1788 (the Vietnamese lunar year Mậu Thân); the decisive fighting took place on 28–30 January 1789.

summary.en: The largest volcanic eruption in recorded history devastated Sumbawa, killing tens of thousands directly and through famine. Its aerosols cooled the northern hemisphere, causing the "Year Without a Summer" of 1816.
summary.zh: 有记录以来规模最大的火山喷发摧毁了松巴哇岛，直接或因饥荒死亡者数以万计。喷发的气溶胶使北半球降温，导致1816年出现“无夏之年”。

sources.title: Clive Oppenheimer, "Climatic, environmental and human consequences of the largest known historic eruption: Tambora volcano (Indonesia) 1815", Progress in Physical Geography 27:2 (2003)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora

story.en:
Mount Tambora on Sumbawa had been quiet for centuries when it began to rumble in 1812. On the evening of 10 April 1815 it exploded. Witnesses saw three columns of fire rise and merge; pyroclastic flows swept down to the sea, wiping out the small kingdoms of Tambora and Pekat, and the mountain lost over a kilometre of its height. The blasts were heard in Sumatra, more than 2,000 km away, and British officers in Java thought they were hearing cannon.

Ash fell for days across the region, destroying crops on Sumbawa and Lombok; Raffles's government later estimated that tens of thousands died of starvation and disease. Excavations at the buried village of Tambora have found houses, pottery and bodies under the ash, a "Pompeii of the East".

The sulphate veil the eruption pushed into the stratosphere cooled the northern hemisphere. 1816 became the "Year Without a Summer": snow fell in New England in June, harvests failed across Europe, and in a cold, stormy Swiss summer Mary Shelley began Frankenstein.
story.zh:
松巴哇岛上的坦博拉火山沉寂了几个世纪，1812年开始发出隆隆声。1815年4月10日傍晚，它猛烈爆发。目击者看到三道火柱升起并汇合；火山碎屑流冲向大海，抹去了坦博拉和佩卡特两个小王国，山体高度降低了一千多米。爆炸声远在两千多公里外的苏门答腊都能听见，驻爪哇的英国军官还以为是炮声。

火山灰连日降落在整个地区，毁坏了松巴哇和龙目的庄稼；莱佛士的政府后来估计，数以万计的人死于饥荒和疾病。在被掩埋的坦博拉村遗址中，考古人员在火山灰下发现了房屋、陶器和遗骸，称之为“东方的庞贝”。

喷发推入平流层的硫酸盐气溶胶使北半球降温。1816年成为“无夏之年”：新英格兰六月飘雪，欧洲各地歉收；在瑞士那个寒冷多风暴的夏天，玛丽·雪莱开始写作《弗兰肯斯坦》。

summary.en: Prince Diponegoro of Yogyakarta led a widespread rebellion against Dutch colonial rule and its Javanese allies. The war cost some 200,000 Javanese lives before Diponegoro was seized at negotiations and exiled.
summary.zh: 日惹王子蒂博尼哥罗领导了一场反抗荷兰殖民统治及其爪哇盟友的大规模起义。战争造成约二十万爪哇人死亡，最终蒂博尼哥罗在谈判中被扣押并流放。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Java War
Peter Carey, The Power of Prophecy: Prince Dipanagara and the End of an Old Order in Java, 1785–1855 (KITLV, 2007)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Java War

summary.en: A cataclysmic eruption destroyed most of Krakatoa island in the Sunda Strait. Tsunamis killed more than 36,000 people on Java and Sumatra, and the explosion was heard thousands of kilometres away.
summary.zh: 巽他海峡的喀拉喀托岛发生灾难性喷发，岛屿大部被摧毁。引发的海啸在爪哇和苏门答腊造成三万六千余人死亡，爆炸声远传数千公里。

sources.title: G. J. Symons (ed.), The Eruption of Krakatoa and Subsequent Phenomena (Royal Society, 1888)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa

story.en:
Krakatoa, an uninhabited volcanic island in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, began erupting in May 1883, and for weeks steamers passing through reported ash and pumice. On the morning of 27 August a series of enormous explosions destroyed most of the island. The last was heard on Rodrigues island, near Mauritius, nearly 4,800 km away, perhaps the loudest sound in recorded history.

The collapse sent tsunamis up to 30 metres high into the coasts of the strait. They swept away the towns of Anyer and Merak and nearly 300 villages; a Dutch gunboat was carried far inland. More than 36,000 people died, most of them drowned. Pressure waves from the blast circled the globe several times and were recorded by barometers worldwide.

For months afterwards, fine ash in the upper atmosphere caused vivid red sunsets across the world. Telegraph cables carried the news to Europe within hours, making Krakatoa the first global media disaster. In 1927 a new volcano, Anak Krakatau, "child of Krakatoa", rose from the sea where the island had been.
story.zh:
喀拉喀托是爪哇与苏门答腊之间巽他海峡中的一座无人火山岛，1883年5月开始喷发，此后数周过往轮船不断报告看到火山灰和浮石。8月27日上午，一连串巨大的爆炸摧毁了岛屿的大部分。最后一次爆炸声远在近4800公里外、毛里求斯附近的罗德里格斯岛都能听到，可能是有史以来最响的声音。

岛体塌陷掀起高达30米的海啸，冲上海峡两岸，卷走了安耶尔、默拉克等城镇和近三百个村庄，一艘荷兰炮舰被冲到远处的内陆。三万六千多人遇难，大多是溺亡。爆炸产生的气压波环绕地球数周，被世界各地的气压计记录下来。

此后数月，高空的细微火山灰使全世界出现绚丽的红色晚霞。电报在几小时内把消息传到欧洲，使喀拉喀托成为第一场全球媒体灾难。1927年，一座新火山“喀拉喀托之子”从原岛所在的海面升起。

summary.en: The secret society Katipunan under Andrés Bonifacio launched an armed revolt against Spain in August 1896; the execution of José Rizal fuelled it. Led later by Emilio Aguinaldo, revolutionaries declared independence on 12 June 1898.
summary.zh: 1896年8月，安德烈斯·博尼法西奥领导的秘密组织卡蒂普南发动反抗西班牙的武装起义，黎刹遭处决更激化了革命。后在埃米利奥·阿奎纳多领导下，革命者于1898年6月12日宣布独立。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Philippine Revolution
Teodoro A. Agoncillo, The Revolt of the Masses: The Story of Bonifacio and the Katipunan (1956)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 2: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries (1992)
Wikipedia: Philippine Revolution

story.en:
The revolution grew out of a generation of reformers. Filipino students in Spain, the ilustrados, campaigned in the 1880s for equal rights and the expulsion of the friars; José Rizal's novels Noli Me Tángere and El Filibusterismo exposed colonial abuses. When Rizal was exiled in 1892, Andrés Bonifacio founded the Katipunan to win independence by arms instead.

Discovered in August 1896, the Katipunan rose around Manila. The Spanish executed Rizal by firing squad at Bagumbayan on 30 December 1896, although he had not supported the revolt, and made him its martyr. In Cavite the rebels under Emilio Aguinaldo won early victories; a bitter rivalry ended with Bonifacio's execution in May 1897, and in December Aguinaldo accepted the truce of Biak-na-Bato and went into exile in Hong Kong.

The Spanish–American War revived the cause. Aguinaldo returned on an American ship in May 1898, rebel armies took most of Luzon, and on 12 June he declared independence at Kawit. But the Americans took Manila for themselves in August, setting up the war that followed.
story.zh:
这场革命源于一代改革者。19世纪80年代，在西班牙留学的菲律宾学生“开明派”呼吁平等权利和驱逐修士；黎刹的小说《不许犯我》和《起义者》揭露了殖民统治的种种弊端。1892年黎刹被流放后，安德烈斯·博尼法西奥创立卡蒂普南，转而谋求以武力争取独立。

1896年8月卡蒂普南暴露，在马尼拉周边起义。尽管黎刹并不支持起义，西班牙人仍于1896年12月30日在巴贡巴扬将他枪决，使他成为革命的殉道者。在甲米地，阿奎纳多领导的起义军初战告捷；一场激烈的内部斗争以1897年5月博尼法西奥被处决告终，同年12月阿奎纳多接受破石洞停战协议，流亡香港。

美西战争使革命重新燃起。1898年5月阿奎纳多乘美国军舰回国，起义军占领吕宋大部，6月12日他在卡维特宣布独立。但美国人在8月独自占领马尼拉，为随后的战争埋下伏笔。

summary.en: The People's Party, a group of military officers and civilian officials, staged a bloodless coup in Bangkok that ended absolute monarchy and gave Siam its first constitution under King Prajadhipok.
summary.zh: 由军官与文官组成的民党在曼谷发动不流血政变，结束了君主专制，在巴差提勃国王治下颁布暹罗第一部宪法。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Siamese revolution of 1932
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Siamese revolution of 1932

summary.en: Two days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta read a brief proclamation of independence at Sukarno's house in Jakarta. Four years of war and diplomacy followed before the Netherlands transferred sovereignty in 1949.
summary.zh: 日本投降两天后，苏加诺与穆罕默德·哈达在雅加达苏加诺寓所宣读简短的独立宣言。此后经过四年的战争与外交斗争，荷兰才于1949年移交主权。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
J. D. Legge, Sukarno: A Political Biography (Allen Lane, 1972)
Wikipedia: Proclamation of Indonesian Independence

story.en:
Japan surrendered on 15 August 1945, but in Java its army still held power. Young radicals in Jakarta, impatient with Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta's caution, kidnapped the two leaders on 16 August and took them to Rengasdengklok to press them to declare independence at once. Returned to the city that night, they drafted a short text in the house of a Japanese admiral, Maeda Tadashi.

At ten in the morning of 17 August, on the veranda of Sukarno's house at Pegangsaan Timur 56, Sukarno read the two-sentence proclamation, signed by himself and Hatta "in the name of the Indonesian people". A red-and-white flag sewn by his wife Fatmawati was raised. The next day Sukarno was named president and Hatta vice-president.

The Dutch, returning with British help, did not accept it. Four years of revolution followed: the battle of Surabaya in November 1945, two Dutch "police actions" and a civil war within the republic. Under American and UN pressure, the Netherlands transferred sovereignty on 27 December 1949, recognising 17 August as the date only in 2023.
story.zh:
日本于1945年8月15日投降，但其军队仍控制着爪哇。雅加达的激进青年不满苏加诺和穆罕默德·哈达的谨慎，8月16日将两人绑架到仁加斯登格洛，逼他们立即宣布独立。当晚回城后，他们在日本海军少将前田精的宅邸起草了一份简短文本。

8月17日上午十时，苏加诺在东伯冈沙安路56号自家门廊前宣读了只有两句话的宣言，由他和哈达“代表印度尼西亚人民”签署，并升起了妻子法特玛瓦蒂缝制的红白旗。次日苏加诺被推举为总统，哈达为副总统。

在英国协助下卷土重来的荷兰人不予承认。此后经历了四年革命：1945年11月的泗水之战、荷兰的两次“警察行动”以及共和国内部的内战。在美国和联合国的压力下，荷兰于1949年12月27日移交主权，直到2023年才承认8月17日为独立日期。

summary.en: At Ba Đình Square in Hanoi, Hồ Chí Minh proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after the August Revolution, quoting the US Declaration of Independence. France's return to Indochina led to war the following year.
summary.zh: 八月革命后，胡志明在河内巴亭广场宣布越南民主共和国成立，并引用了美国《独立宣言》的语句。法国重返印度支那，次年爆发战争。

sources.title: Hồ Chí Minh, Tuyên ngôn độc lập (Declaration of Independence), 2 September 1945
William J. Duiker, Ho Chi Minh: A Life (Hyperion, 2000)
Wikipedia: Declaration of independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam

story.en:
In August 1945, as Japan surrendered, the Viet Minh launched a general uprising. Within two weeks it controlled Hanoi, Huế and Saigon, and Emperor Bảo Đại abdicated, handing his seal and sword to a Viet Minh delegation and calling himself a citizen of a free country.

On 2 September, before a crowd in Ba Đình Square estimated at hundreds of thousands, Hồ Chí Minh read the declaration of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam. He opened by quoting the American Declaration of Independence that all men are created equal, and then the French Declaration of the Rights of Man, before listing the crimes of French colonial rule. American OSS officers were present, and their planes flew overhead.

The new state was fragile. Chinese Nationalist troops occupied the north to disarm the Japanese, British forces in the south helped the French back into Saigon, and famine had killed perhaps a million people in the north that year. Within sixteen months the Democratic Republic was at war with France.
story.zh:
1945年8月日本投降之际，越盟发动总起义。两周之内，它控制了河内、顺化和西贡；保大皇帝退位，把玉玺和宝剑交给越盟代表团，并自称“一个自由国家的公民”。

9月2日，在巴亭广场据估计数十万人的人群面前，胡志明宣读了越南民主共和国独立宣言。他首先引用美国《独立宣言》中“人人生而平等”的语句，又引用法国《人权宣言》，随后列举法国殖民统治的罪行。美国战略情报局人员在场，美国飞机从上空飞过。

新生国家十分脆弱。中国国民党军队进驻北方解除日军武装，南方的英军则帮助法国人重返西贡；当年的饥荒在北方夺去了约一百万人的生命。不到十六个月，越南民主共和国便与法国开战。

summary.en: Việt Minh forces under Võ Nguyên Giáp hauled artillery onto the hills around a French fortified valley and forced its surrender after 56 days. The defeat ended French rule in Indochina at the Geneva Conference.
summary.zh: 武元甲指挥越盟军队将火炮运上环绕法军谷地要塞的山头，经五十六天围攻迫使守军投降。此役使法国在日内瓦会议上结束了对印度支那的统治。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Điện Biên Phủ
Bernard B. Fall, Hell in a Very Small Place: The Siege of Dien Bien Phu (Lippincott, 1966)
Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War: The Fall of an Empire and the Making of America's Vietnam (Random House, 2012)
Wikipedia: Battle of Dien Bien Phu

story.en:
In November 1953 French paratroopers dropped into the valley of Điện Biên Phủ, near the Lao border, to block Viet Minh moves into Laos and to tempt Võ Nguyên Giáp into a pitched battle. The commander, Colonel de Castries, ringed the airstrip with strongpoints, reportedly given women's names. French planners assumed the enemy could not bring heavy artillery through the mountains.

They were wrong. Tens of thousands of porters with bicycles and pack animals carried supplies along jungle tracks, and Viet Minh troops dragged dismantled guns, many supplied by China, onto the hillsides and dug them in. The bombardment that opened on 13 March 1954 overran Béatrice and Gabrielle within days and closed the airstrip; the French artillery commander, Colonel Piroth, killed himself.

For 56 days the defenders fought in flooded trenches, supplied by parachute. The last positions fell on 7 May, and about 11,000 French Union troops were taken prisoner. The next day the Geneva Conference turned to Indochina, and in July it divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel.
story.zh:
1953年11月，法国伞兵空降到靠近老挝边境的奠边府河谷，意在阻断越盟进入老挝，并引诱武元甲打一场阵地战。指挥官德卡斯特里上校在机场周围修建了一圈据点，据说都以女性名字命名。法军参谋们认为敌人无法把重炮运过群山。

他们错了。数以万计的民工推着自行车、赶着驮畜沿丛林小道运送物资，越盟士兵把拆散的大炮（许多由中国提供）拖上山坡并挖掘炮位。1954年3月13日炮击开始，几天内就攻下了“贝亚特丽丝”和“加布丽埃勒”据点，切断了机场；法军炮兵指挥官皮罗特上校自杀。

守军在积水的战壕里苦战56天，依靠空投补给。最后的阵地于5月7日陷落，约一万一千名法兰西联邦军队官兵被俘。次日日内瓦会议开始讨论印度支那问题，7月会议以北纬17度线分割越南。

summary.en: A war between communist North Vietnam with the southern National Liberation Front and the US-backed South Vietnam. US troop strength passed 500,000 in 1968 and peaked at about 543,000 in 1969; after the US withdrawal of 1973, Saigon fell in April 1975 and Vietnam was reunified.
summary.zh: 以越南北方及南方民族解放阵线为一方、美国支持的南越为另一方的战争。美军在越兵力于1968年超过五十万，1969年达到约54.3万的峰值；1973年美军撤出后，西贡于1975年4月陷落，越南实现统一。

label.en: US Marines land at Đà Nẵng
label.zh: 美国海军陆战队登陆岘港

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Vietnam War
Stanley Karnow, Vietnam: A History (Viking, 1983)
Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War: The Fall of an Empire and the Making of America's Vietnam (Random House, 2012)
Wikipedia: Vietnam War

note: Point plotted at Huế, near the former partition line; the war was fought across Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia.

story.en:
The Geneva Accords of 1954 divided Vietnam pending elections that were never held. In the south Ngô Đình Diệm built an anti-communist state with American aid; from 1959 Hanoi backed an insurgency there, organised from 1960 as the National Liberation Front. After the Gulf of Tonkin incident of 1964 the United States began bombing the north, and in March 1965 the first combat Marines landed at Đà Nẵng.

American strategy relied on firepower and attrition: search-and-destroy missions, chemical defoliation and the heaviest bombing campaign in history up to that time. The communists answered with the Hồ Chí Minh Trail through Laos and Cambodia and were supplied by the Soviet Union and China. The Tet Offensive of 1968 convinced many Americans that the war could not be won, and President Nixon began "Vietnamisation".

The Paris Peace Accords of January 1973 withdrew US forces. Two years later the northern offensive overran the south, and Saigon fell on 30 April 1975. Estimates of Vietnamese dead range from about one million to more than three million; some 58,000 Americans and hundreds of thousands of Laotians and Cambodians also died.
story.zh:
1954年的日内瓦协议暂时分割越南，待日后举行选举，但选举从未举行。在南方，吴庭艳在美国援助下建立反共国家；1959年起，河内支持南方的武装斗争，1960年组成民族解放阵线。1964年北部湾事件后，美国开始轰炸北方，1965年3月首批作战陆战队在岘港登陆。

美国的战略依赖火力与消耗：“搜索与摧毁”行动、化学落叶剂，以及当时史上规模最大的轰炸。共产党方面则依靠穿越老挝和柬埔寨的胡志明小道，并得到苏联和中国的补给。1968年春节攻势使许多美国人相信战争无法取胜，尼克松总统开始推行“越南化”。

1973年1月的《巴黎和平协定》使美军撤出。两年后北方发动攻势席卷南方，西贡于1975年4月30日陷落。越南死亡人数的估计从约一百万到三百多万不等；另有约五万八千名美国人以及数十万老挝人和柬埔寨人丧生。

summary.en: North Vietnamese torpedo boats clashed with the USS Maddox on 2 August; a second reported attack on 4 August probably never happened. Congress's resulting Gulf of Tonkin Resolution authorised escalation of the war.
summary.zh: 8月2日北越鱼雷艇与美舰“马多克斯”号交火；8月4日所报告的第二次袭击很可能并未发生。随后国会通过《北部湾决议》，授权战争升级。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Gulf of Tonkin incident
Stanley Karnow, Vietnam: A History (Viking, 1983)
Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War: The Fall of an Empire and the Making of America's Vietnam (Random House, 2012)
Wikipedia: Gulf of Tonkin incident

summary.en: The foreign ministers of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand signed the Bangkok Declaration, creating the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to promote regional cooperation and stability.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚、马来西亚、菲律宾、新加坡和泰国外长签署《曼谷宣言》，成立东南亚国家联盟，以促进区域合作与稳定。

sources.title: The ASEAN Declaration (Bangkok Declaration), 8 August 1967
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 2: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries (1992)
Wikipedia: ASEAN Declaration

story.en:
In August 1967 the foreign ministers of five countries met at a seaside resort at Bang Saen, south of Bangkok, for what they later called "sports-shirt diplomacy": golf and informal talks. Only a year earlier Indonesia had been waging Konfrontasi against Malaysia, and the Philippines still claimed Sabah. The Thai foreign minister, Thanat Khoman, had brokered their reconciliation.

On 8 August, at the Thai foreign ministry, Adam Malik of Indonesia, Narciso Ramos of the Philippines, Tun Abdul Razak of Malaysia, S. Rajaratnam of Singapore and Thanat signed a two-page Bangkok Declaration founding the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. It spoke of economic growth, social progress and cultural development, but its unspoken purpose was to keep the region out of great-power conflict as the Vietnam War raged.

ASEAN grew slowly, working by consensus and non-interference, the "ASEAN way". Brunei joined in 1984, Vietnam in 1995, Laos and Myanmar in 1997, Cambodia in 1999 and Timor-Leste in 2025, bringing every country of the region into the association.
story.zh:
1967年8月，五国外长在曼谷以南的邦盛海滨度假地会面，开展了他们后来所称的“运动衫外交”：打高尔夫、非正式会谈。仅仅一年前，印尼还在对马来西亚实行“对抗”政策，菲律宾仍坚持对沙巴的主权要求。泰国外长他纳·科曼促成了各方和解。

8月8日，印尼的亚当·马利克、菲律宾的纳西索·拉莫斯、马来西亚的敦·阿卜杜勒·拉扎克、新加坡的拉惹勒南和他纳在泰国外交部签署了只有两页的《曼谷宣言》，成立东南亚国家联盟。宣言谈的是经济增长、社会进步和文化发展，但其未明言的目的，是在越战正酣之际使本地区免受大国冲突的波及。

东盟发展缓慢，以协商一致和互不干涉为原则，即所谓“东盟方式”。文莱于1984年加入，越南1995年，老挝和缅甸1997年，柬埔寨1999年，东帝汶于2025年加入，至此本地区所有国家都成为成员。

summary.en: During the Tết truce, communist forces attacked more than 100 towns across South Vietnam, including the US embassy in Saigon and the old capital Huế. A military failure for the attackers, it was a political turning point that eroded American support for the war.
summary.zh: 在春节休战期间，共产党军队对南越一百多个城镇发动进攻，包括西贡美国大使馆和古都顺化。进攻在军事上失利，却成为政治转折点，削弱了美国国内对战争的支持。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tet Offensive
Stanley Karnow, Vietnam: A History (Viking, 1983)
Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War: The Fall of an Empire and the Making of America's Vietnam (Random House, 2012)
Wikipedia: Tet Offensive

note: Point at the US embassy in Saigon, attacked in the first hours; the offensive struck more than 100 towns, and the longest battle was at Huế.

story.en:
For the lunar new year of 1968 both sides had announced a truce. In the early hours of 31 January some 80,000 communist troops attacked more than a hundred cities and towns across South Vietnam at once. In Saigon a team of sappers blew a hole in the wall of the US embassy compound and fought in its grounds for six hours.

The planners in Hanoi, led by Lê Duẩn, had hoped to spark a general uprising. It did not happen, and the attackers were driven back almost everywhere with very heavy losses. In Huế, however, they held the old citadel for nearly a month, and during the occupation they executed some 2,800 or more civilians and officials; American and South Vietnamese counter-attacks levelled much of the city. At Khe Sanh a besieged Marine base held out.

Militarily Tet was a communist defeat, but in the United States it destroyed confidence in official claims of progress. Walter Cronkite told viewers the war was a stalemate; in March Lyndon Johnson halted most bombing of the north and announced he would not seek re-election.
story.zh:
1968年农历新年，双方都宣布停火。1月31日凌晨，约八万名共产党部队同时袭击南越一百多座城镇。在西贡，一支工兵小组在美国大使馆围墙上炸开缺口，在院内激战六个小时。

以黎笋为首的河内策划者原希望引发全面起义，但起义并未发生，进攻者几乎在各地都被击退，损失极为惨重。不过在顺化，他们占据旧皇城近一个月，期间处决了约二千八百名或更多平民和官员；美军和南越军的反攻也把城市大部分夷为平地。在溪山，被围的陆战队基地坚守了下来。

从军事上看，春节攻势是共产党方面的失败，但在美国，它摧毁了民众对官方宣称“战事进展顺利”的信任。沃尔特·克朗凯特告诉观众战争已陷入僵局；3月，林登·约翰逊停止了对北方的大部分轰炸，并宣布不再寻求连任。

name.en: Khmer Rouge rule and the Cambodian genocide
name.zh: 红色高棉统治与柬埔寨大屠杀

summary.en: After taking Phnom Penh on 17 April 1975, the Khmer Rouge emptied the cities and forced the population into agrarian labour camps. Execution, starvation and disease killed roughly 1.5–2 million people before Vietnam's invasion ended the regime in January 1979.
summary.zh: 1975年4月17日攻占金边后，红色高棉驱散城市居民，强迫全体民众进入农业劳动营。处决、饥饿和疾病造成约一百五十万至二百万人死亡，直至1979年1月越南出兵推翻该政权。

sources.title: Ben Kiernan, The Pol Pot Regime: Race, Power, and Genocide in Cambodia under the Khmer Rouge, 1975–79 (Yale University Press, 1996)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Documentation Center of Cambodia (DC-Cam)
Wikipedia: Cambodian genocide

note: Death-toll estimates range from about 1.5 to over 2 million; coordinates mark the Choeung Ek killing field.

story.en:
On 17 April 1975 Khmer Rouge soldiers, many of them teenagers from the countryside, marched into Phnom Penh. Within days they ordered the entire population, some two million people swollen by refugees, to leave, claiming the Americans would bomb the city. Hospitals were emptied; those who could not walk died on the roads.

The Communist Party of Kampuchea, calling itself simply Angkar, "the organisation", declared Year Zero. Money, markets, schools, religion and private property were abolished, and families were broken up into work brigades digging irrigation canals and growing rice on impossible quotas. "New people" from the towns were treated as enemies. Former officials, teachers, monks, ethnic Vietnamese, Cham Muslims and, increasingly, party members suspected of treason were killed. At the Tuol Sleng school in Phnom Penh, prison S-21, some 14,000 people were photographed, tortured into confessions and sent to the killing fields at Choeung Ek; only a handful survived.

By most estimates between 1.5 and 2 million people, roughly a quarter of the population, died. Vietnam's invasion ended the regime in January 1979. A UN-backed tribunal convicted the prison chief Duch and the senior leaders Nuon Chea and Khieu Samphan; Pol Pot died before he could be tried.
story.zh:
1975年4月17日，红色高棉士兵开进金边，其中许多是来自农村的十几岁少年。几天之内，他们以美国即将轰炸为由，命令全城约两百万居民（因难民涌入而大增）全部撤离。医院被清空，无法行走的人死在路上。

自称“组织”（安卡）的柬埔寨共产党宣布“零年”。货币、市场、学校、宗教和私有财产全部废除，家庭被拆散编入劳动队，挖掘灌溉渠、按无法完成的定额种植水稻。来自城镇的“新人”被视为敌人。前官员、教师、僧侣、越南族人、占族穆斯林，以及越来越多被怀疑叛变的党员遭到杀害。在金边的吐斯廉中学，即S-21监狱，约一万四千人被拍照、刑讯逼供，然后被送往钟屋克的“杀戮场”，生还者寥寥无几。

据多数估计，约150万至200万人死亡，大约占全国人口的四分之一。1979年1月越南入侵终结了这一政权。联合国支持的特别法庭判处监狱长杜赫以及高层领导人农谢和乔森潘有罪；波尔布特在受审前就已死去。

summary.en: North Vietnamese tanks crashed through the gates of the Independence Palace as the last Americans were evacuated by helicopter. The surrender of South Vietnam ended the war; Saigon was renamed Ho Chi Minh City in 1976.
summary.zh: 北越坦克冲破独立宫大门，最后一批美国人乘直升机撤离。南越投降，战争结束；1976年西贡改名为胡志明市。

sources.title: Stanley Karnow, Vietnam: A History (Viking, 1983)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Fall of Saigon

story.en:
In March 1975 North Vietnam launched what it expected to be the first stage of a two-year offensive. Instead South Vietnam's army collapsed: President Thiệu ordered the Central Highlands abandoned, and the retreat became a rout. Huế and Đà Nẵng fell within weeks, and by late April some fifteen divisions were closing on Saigon. Thiệu resigned and fled.

On 29 April the United States began Operation Frequent Wind, the largest helicopter evacuation in history. Over eighteen hours some 7,000 Americans and South Vietnamese were flown out to ships offshore, while crowds besieged the embassy; the last Marines lifted off its roof early on 30 April. At sea, South Vietnamese pilots landed on carriers, and crews pushed helicopters overboard to make room.

Around noon on 30 April a North Vietnamese tank smashed through the gates of the Independence Palace. General Dương Văn Minh, president for two days, said he was waiting to transfer power; a northern officer told him he had nothing left to transfer. The war was over, and Vietnam was formally reunified in 1976.
story.zh:
1975年3月，北越发动了原以为是两年攻势第一阶段的进攻。南越军队却迅速崩溃：阮文绍总统下令放弃西原，撤退演变为溃败。顺化和岘港在数周内相继失守，到4月下旬，约十五个师逼近西贡。阮文绍辞职出逃。

4月29日，美国开始执行“常风行动”，这是史上规模最大的直升机撤离行动。十八个小时内，约七千名美国人和南越人被运到外海的军舰上，人群则包围了大使馆；最后一批陆战队员于30日凌晨从使馆楼顶起飞。海上，南越飞行员驾机降落在航空母舰上，水兵们把直升机推下海以腾出甲板。

4月30日中午前后，一辆北越坦克撞开独立宫的大门。上任仅两天的总统杨文明说，他正在等待移交权力；一名北方军官告诉他，他已没有什么可移交的了。战争结束，越南于1976年正式统一。

summary.en: After a fraudulent snap election, a military revolt and millions of peaceful protesters on Manila's EDSA avenue forced President Ferdinand Marcos into exile, bringing Corazon Aquino to power.
summary.zh: 在舞弊的提前选举之后，军方哗变与数百万和平示威者聚集马尼拉乙沙大道，迫使总统费迪南德·马科斯流亡，科拉松·阿基诺就任总统。

sources.title: Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 2: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries (1992)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ferdinand Marcos
Wikipedia: People Power Revolution

summary.en: A magnitude 9.1 megathrust earthquake off northern Sumatra sent tsunamis across the Indian Ocean, killing about 230,000 people in 14 countries; Aceh in Indonesia suffered most.
summary.zh: 苏门答腊北部近海发生9.1级逆冲型大地震，引发的海啸横扫印度洋，在十四个国家造成约二十三万人死亡，其中印度尼西亚亚齐受灾最为惨重。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
U.S. Geological Survey, M 9.1 – 2004 Sumatra–Andaman Islands Earthquake (event summary)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami

story.en:
At 7:58 on the morning of 26 December 2004, the seafloor west of northern Sumatra ruptured along some 1,300 km of the boundary between the India and Burma plates. The magnitude 9.1 earthquake, the third-largest ever recorded, lasted up to ten minutes and lifted the seabed by several metres.

Within about twenty minutes waves up to 30 metres high struck the coast of Aceh. Much of Banda Aceh and the town of Meulaboh were destroyed, and about 170,000 people died in Indonesia alone. Over the following hours the tsunami crossed the Indian Ocean, killing people in Thailand, Sri Lanka, India, the Maldives and as far as Somalia. There was no warning system in the Indian Ocean. A ten-year-old British girl on Maikhao beach in Thailand, Tilly Smith, recognised the receding sea from a geography lesson and helped clear the beach.

About 230,000 people died in fourteen countries. The disaster led to an Indian Ocean tsunami warning system, and in Aceh it helped end a thirty-year separatist war: the Helsinki peace agreement was signed in August 2005.
story.zh:
2004年12月26日早晨7时58分，苏门答腊北部以西的海底沿印度板块与缅甸板块边界约1300公里发生破裂。这次9.1级地震是有记录以来第三大地震，持续长达十分钟，海床抬升数米。

大约二十分钟内，高达30米的巨浪袭击亚齐海岸。班达亚齐大部和默拉务镇被毁，仅印尼就有约17万人遇难。此后数小时内，海啸横越印度洋，在泰国、斯里兰卡、印度、马尔代夫，远至索马里都造成伤亡。当时印度洋没有任何预警系统。在泰国迈考海滩，一名十岁的英国女孩蒂莉·史密斯根据地理课上学到的知识认出了海水退潮的征兆，帮助疏散了海滩上的人。

这场灾难在十四个国家造成约23万人死亡，促成了印度洋海啸预警系统的建立。在亚齐，它还促使一场持续三十年的分离主义战争走向终结：2005年8月双方签署了赫尔辛基和平协议。

summary.en: Excavations at Óc Eo in the Mekong delta revealed a canal-linked port city of Funan with Roman coins, including a gold piece of Antoninus Pius, Indian seals, Chinese bronze mirrors and local goldwork. It shows the maritime trade that linked the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea from the 2nd to 6th centuries.
summary.zh: 在湄公河三角洲俄厄的发掘揭示出一座以运河相连的扶南港口城市，出土有罗马钱币（包括安敦宁·毕尤的金币）、印度印章、中国铜镜和本地金饰，展现了2至6世纪连接印度洋与南海的海上贸易。

sources.title: Britannica: Oc Eo
Wikipedia: Óc Eo
Louis Malleret, L'Archéologie du delta du Mékong (1959–63)

note: Span approximate: the Antoninus Pius coin is dated 152; the site declined with Funan in the 6th century.

summary.en: The court poet Mpu Prapanca composed this Old Javanese eulogy of King Hayam Wuruk in 1365, describing the Majapahit capital, royal progresses and a list of tributary lands across the archipelago. A palm-leaf copy found at Cakranegara on Lombok in 1894 is on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register.
summary.zh: 宫廷诗人普拉潘扎于1365年用古爪哇语创作这部颂扬国王哈亚·乌鲁克的长诗，描述满者伯夷都城、王室巡游以及遍布群岛的属地名单。1894年在龙目岛查克拉内加拉发现的贝叶抄本已列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》。

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World: Nāgarakrětāgama or Description of the Country (1365 AD)
Wikipedia: Nagarakretagama
Th. G. Th. Pigeaud, Java in the 14th Century: A Study in Cultural History (1960–63)

note: Marker at Trowulan, generally identified as the Majapahit capital the poem describes (the identification is not proven archaeologically); Wikidata's coordinates are those of the National Library in Jakarta, which holds the manuscript.

summary.en: After Andrés de Urdaneta found the eastward return route across the Pacific in 1565, Spanish galleons sailed between Manila and Acapulco for 250 years, exchanging Chinese silk and porcelain for Mexican and Peruvian silver. The trade tied Asia to the Americas and made silver a global currency.
summary.zh: 1565年乌尔达内塔找到横渡太平洋东返的航线后，西班牙大帆船250年间往返于马尼拉和阿卡普尔科之间，以中国丝绸和瓷器换取墨西哥和秘鲁的白银。这一贸易把亚洲与美洲连接起来，使白银成为全球通货。

sources.title: Britannica: Manila galleon
Wikipedia: Manila galleon
Dennis O. Flynn & Arturo Giráldez, "Born with a Silver Spoon: The Origin of World Trade in 1571", Journal of World History 6 (1995)

note: The first return voyage left Cebu in 1565; Manila became the Asian terminus after its founding in 1571, and the last galleon sailed in 1815.

story.en:
Spanish ships had crossed the Pacific westward since Magellan, but none could find a way back until 1565, when the friar-navigator Andrés de Urdaneta sailed north to about 40 degrees, caught the westerlies and reached California and then Acapulco. From 1565 until 1815 one or two great galleons a year made the round trip between Manila and Acapulco.

The cargoes were fabulous. Eastbound galleons carried Chinese silk, porcelain and lacquer, Indian cotton and spices, bought in Manila from Chinese junks; westbound they carried Mexican and Peruvian silver. The voyage to Acapulco took four to six months, and scurvy and typhoons killed many crews; the wreck of the San José in 1694 and the capture of the Nuestra Señora de Covadonga by the English in 1743 were famous losses.

Historians see the galleon route as the moment the world economy became truly global: silver from Potosí paid for Chinese goods and much of it ended up in China, while Asian goods, plants and people, including Filipino sailors who settled in Mexico, crossed to the Americas.
story.zh:
自麦哲伦以来，西班牙船只一直能向西横渡太平洋，却始终找不到回程航线，直到1565年，修士兼航海家安德烈斯·德乌尔达内塔北上到约北纬40度，借西风抵达加利福尼亚，再到阿卡普尔科。从1565年到1815年，每年有一两艘大帆船往返于马尼拉与阿卡普尔科之间。

货物价值惊人。东行的帆船满载在马尼拉从中国帆船购得的中国丝绸、瓷器和漆器，以及印度棉布和香料；西行则运载墨西哥和秘鲁的白银。驶往阿卡普尔科的航程长达四到六个月，坏血病和台风夺去了许多船员的生命；1694年“圣何塞”号沉没和1743年“科瓦东加圣母”号被英国人俘获都是著名的损失。

史学家认为，大帆船航线标志着世界经济真正走向全球化：波托西的白银用来购买中国货物，其中大量最终流入中国；亚洲的商品、植物和人口（包括定居墨西哥的菲律宾水手）则跨洋来到美洲。

summary.en: After reawakening in April, Pinatubo on Luzon produced the second-largest eruption of the 20th century on 15 June 1991, as a typhoon passed. Forecasts by Philippine and US volcanologists allowed mass evacuations that saved thousands of lives; the sulphur cloud cooled the globe by about 0.5 °C.
summary.zh: 皮纳图博火山于4月重新活跃，1991年6月15日在台风过境时发生20世纪第二大规模的喷发。菲律宾和美国火山学家的预报促成了大规模疏散，挽救了数以千计的生命；喷出的硫化物云使全球气温下降约0.5°C。

sources.title: USGS Fact Sheet 113-97: The Cataclysmic 1991 Eruption of Mount Pinatubo, Philippines
Britannica: Mount Pinatubo
Wikipedia: 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo

name.en: Tomb of Sultan Malik al-Salih of Samudera Pasai
name.zh: 须文答剌-巴赛苏丹马利克·萨利赫墓

summary.en: The gravestone of Malik al-Salih, first Muslim ruler of Samudera Pasai in northern Sumatra, is dated 696 AH (1297). Marco Polo, passing in 1292, found nearby Perlak already Muslim; Pasai became the first major Islamic sultanate of Southeast Asia, visited by Ibn Battuta in 1345.
summary.zh: 苏门答腊北部须文答剌-巴赛首位穆斯林统治者马利克·萨利赫的墓碑纪年为伊斯兰历696年（1297年）。1292年途经此地的马可·波罗记载附近的八儿剌（佩尔拉克）已信奉伊斯兰教；巴赛成为东南亚第一个重要的伊斯兰苏丹国，1345年伊本·白图泰曾到访。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Samudera Pasai Sultanate
Britannica: Samudra-Pasai
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., 2008)

note: No Wikidata item exists for the tomb or the conversion; the sultanate's QID (a polity) is not reused. Marker at the tomb site at Beuringin, Samudera (Aceh Utara), approximate.

story.en:
Islam reached Southeast Asia along the trade routes, carried by merchants from Gujarat, Arabia and Persia, long before any ruler converted. The first firm evidence of a Muslim kingdom is a gravestone at Samudera, on the north coast of Sumatra: it marks the tomb of Sultan Malik al-Salih, who died in 696 AH, 1297 CE.

According to the Hikayat Raja Pasai, a later Malay chronicle, Merah Silu, a local chief, dreamed that the Prophet spat into his mouth, woke able to recite the Qur'an, and was named Malik al-Salih by a sheikh sent from Mecca. Marco Polo, who waited out the monsoon nearby in 1292, reported that the port of Perlak had become Muslim through contact with "Saracen merchants", while its neighbours had not.

Pasai grew rich on pepper and became a centre of learning. Ibn Battuta stayed there in 1345 on his way to China and was received by Sultan al-Malik al-Zahir, whom he described as devout and fond of debating with scholars. The later rise of Malacca and Aceh eclipsed it, but Pasai is remembered as the first sultanate of the Malay world.
story.zh:
伊斯兰教沿着贸易航线传入东南亚，早在任何统治者皈依之前，古吉拉特、阿拉伯和波斯商人就已把它带到这里。穆斯林王国最早的确凿证据是苏门答腊北岸须文达那的一块墓碑：它标记着苏丹马利克·萨利赫的陵墓，他卒于伊斯兰历696年，即公元1297年。

据后来的马来编年史《巴赛列王传》记载，当地首领默拉·西卢梦见先知向他口中吐唾沫，醒来后便能诵读《古兰经》，一位从麦加派来的长老为他取名马利克·萨利赫。1292年在附近等候季风的马可·波罗记载，八儿剌港已因与“撒拉森商人”接触而改信伊斯兰教，而其邻邦尚未改宗。

巴赛依靠胡椒贸易致富，成为学术中心。1345年伊本·白图泰赴中国途中在此停留，受到苏丹马利克·扎希尔的接见，他形容这位苏丹虔诚并喜欢与学者辩论。后来马六甲和亚齐的兴起使巴赛黯然失色，但它作为马来世界第一个苏丹国而为人铭记。

summary.en: In a valley behind the Cham capital, King Bhadravarman dedicated a wooden shrine to Shiva around 400; for nine centuries Cham kings rebuilt it in brick and stone into some seventy temple towers. American bombing in 1969 destroyed many of them.
summary.zh: 约400年，占婆国王跋陀罗跋摩在都城后方的山谷中建起一座供奉湿婆的木构神殿；此后九个世纪，历代占婆国王以砖石重建扩建，形成约七十座塔庙。1969年美军轰炸摧毁了其中许多建筑。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: My Son Sanctuary
Andrew Hardy, Mauro Cucarzi & Patrizia Zolese (eds.), Champa and the Archaeology of Mỹ Sơn (NUS Press, 2009)
Wikipedia: Mỹ Sơn

note: The first shrine is dated from Bhadravarman's inscriptions to the late 4th or early 5th century.

summary.en: Isanavarman I made Isanapura (Sambor Prei Kuk) the capital of Chenla, raising octagonal brick temples decorated with "flying palaces". The Sui history describes a city of 20,000 households, the largest pre-Angkorian centre in Cambodia.
summary.zh: 伊奢那跋摩一世以伊奢那补罗（三波坡雷古）为真腊都城，修建饰有“飞宫”浮雕的八角形砖塔。《隋书》称其城有二万余家，是柬埔寨吴哥以前最大的中心。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Temple Zone of Sambor Prei Kuk
Sui shu (Book of Sui), "Treatise on Zhenla"
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Sambor Prei Kuk

note: Dates follow Isanavarman I's reign (c. 616–637).

summary.en: The Tang monk Yijing stopped at Srivijaya on his way to India in 671 to learn Sanskrit, and returned in 687 to spend years copying and translating scriptures. His Record of Buddhist Practices, written there, describes over a thousand monks at the Srivijayan court.
summary.zh: 唐代僧人义净于671年赴印度途中在室利佛逝停留学习梵语，687年又返回此地，多年抄写、翻译佛经。他在此写成的《南海寄归内法传》记载，室利佛逝王城有僧侣千余人。

sources.title: Yijing, Nanhai jigui neifa zhuan (A Record of Buddhist Practices Sent Home from the Southern Sea, 691)
O. W. Wolters, Early Indonesian Commerce (Cornell University Press, 1967)
Wikipedia: Yijing (monk)

story.en:
In the winter of 671 Yijing boarded a Persian merchant ship at Guangzhou. Twenty days later he landed at Foshi, Srivijaya, on the Musi river in Sumatra, and stayed six months to study Sanskrit grammar before the king sent him on, in a royal ship, to Malayu and India. He spent more than a decade at Nalanda.

On the way home he stopped again at Srivijaya, and found it the ideal place to work. He advised Chinese monks bound for India to train there first, because its teachers followed the same rules as in India. Running short of paper and ink, he went back to Guangzhou in 689 on a ship that sailed unexpectedly, recruited helpers and returned.

From Srivijaya he sent home his Record of Buddhist Practices and a book of biographies of pilgrim monks. Together they are our best picture of the 7th-century Malay world: a trading kingdom on the monsoon route whose rulers made it a centre of Buddhist learning, a role the Buddhist Talang Tuwo inscription of 684 also reflects.
story.zh:
671年冬，义净在广州登上一艘波斯商船，二十天后抵达苏门答腊穆西河畔的“佛逝”（室利佛逝），停留半年学习梵文文法，随后国王派船送他前往末罗瑜和印度。他在那烂陀寺学习了十余年。

归途中他再次来到室利佛逝，认为这里是译经的理想之地。他建议赴印度求法的中国僧人先在此修学，因为当地的师资和戒律与印度相同。689年他因缺少纸墨，搭上一艘意外起航的商船回到广州，招募助手后又返回室利佛逝。

他从室利佛逝寄回了《南海寄归内法传》和《大唐西域求法高僧传》。这两部书是了解7世纪马来世界最好的资料：一个位于季风航路上的贸易王国，其统治者使之成为佛学中心；684年的佛教达朗图沃碑铭也反映了这一点。

name.zh: 珊阇耶王的康加尔碑铭

summary.en: A Sanskrit inscription on Mount Wukir in Central Java records King Sanjaya's dedication of a Shiva linga in 732. It is the earliest dated record of the Mataram kingdom, whose rulers would build Borobudur and Prambanan.
summary.zh: 中爪哇乌基尔山上的梵文碑铭，记载了732年珊阇耶王供奉湿婆林伽之事。这是马打兰王国最早有确切纪年的记录，该王国后来修建了婆罗浮屠和普兰巴南。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Paul Michel Munoz, Early Kingdoms of the Indonesian Archipelago and the Malay Peninsula (Editions Didier Millet, 2006)
Wikipedia: Canggal inscription

name.zh: 伊洛瓦底江的骠国城邦

summary.en: Beikthano, Halin and Sri Ksetra were walled brick cities with irrigated fields, Buddhist stupas and urn burials, the first urban civilisation of Burma. A Pyu embassy with musicians reached Chang'an in 802; a Nanzhao raid in 832 broke their power.
summary.zh: 毗湿奴城、汉林和室利差呾罗是筑有砖墙、灌溉农田、佛塔与瓮棺葬的城市，是缅甸最早的城市文明。802年骠国使团携乐工抵达长安；832年南诏的劫掠摧毁了骠国的势力。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Pyu Ancient Cities
Xin Tangshu (New Book of Tang), "Treatise on the Piao"
Janice Stargardt, The Ancient Pyu of Burma (Cambridge, 1990)
Wikipedia: Pyu city-states

note: Pinned at Sri Ksetra, the largest city; dates are archaeological estimates. Wikidata's point is at Halin.

name.en: Jayavarman II consecrated on Phnom Kulen
name.zh: 阇耶跋摩二世在荔枝山受封

summary.en: On Mahendraparvata, the Kulen plateau north of Angkor, a Brahmin performed a rite making Jayavarman II a chakravartin, universal monarch, and freeing the Khmer from "Java". The ceremony, recorded 250 years later, is the conventional founding of the Khmer Empire.
summary.zh: 在吴哥以北的荔枝山（摩醯因陀罗山）上，一位婆罗门为阇耶跋摩二世举行仪式，奉其为“转轮王”，宣告高棉摆脱“爪哇”。这一由250年后的碑铭记载的仪式，被视为高棉帝国建立的传统标志。

sources.title: Sdok Kak Thom inscription (K. 235, 1052)
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Damian Evans et al., "Uncovering archaeological landscapes at Angkor using lidar", PNAS 110 (2013)
Wikipedia: Jayavarman II

note: The date 802 rests on the Sdok Kak Thom inscription; the QID is that of the mountain where the rite took place.

story.en:
Almost everything known about the founding of Angkor comes from one stone. In 1052 a family of court priests carved the Sdok Kak Thom inscription to record their own lineage, and in passing told how, two and a half centuries earlier, their ancestor had served a king named Jayavarman who "came from Java".

According to the inscription, Jayavarman spent years moving his court and subduing local lords across Cambodia. Then, on Mahendraparvata, "the mountain of the great Indra", a Brahmin named Hiranyadama performed a rite so that "Kambuja" would no longer depend on Java, and established the cult of the devaraja, the god-king, to be served by the priestly family forever. Historians still argue whether "Java" meant the island, a Malay power, or simply a foreign overlord.

The mountain city of Mahendraparvata itself was lost in the forest until 2012, when airborne lidar revealed a grid of streets, dykes and temples beneath the canopy of Phnom Kulen. Jayavarman later ruled from Hariharalaya, near Angkor, where his successors would build the greatest temple complex in the world.
story.zh:
关于吴哥建国的几乎所有信息都来自一块石碑。1052年，一个宫廷祭司家族刻下斯多卡通碑铭以记录本族世系，其中顺带讲述了两个半世纪前，他们的祖先如何侍奉一位“来自爪哇”的国王阇耶跋摩。

据碑铭记载，阇耶跋摩多年辗转迁移王廷，征服柬埔寨各地的首领。之后，在“大因陀罗之山”摩醯因陀罗山上，婆罗门希兰亚达摩举行仪式，使“甘菩遮”不再依附爪哇，并确立了“神王”崇拜，由这一祭司家族世代奉祀。“爪哇”究竟指爪哇岛、某个马来政权，还是泛指外来宗主，史学家至今争论不休。

摩醯因陀罗山城本身长期湮没于森林之中，直到2012年机载激光雷达在荔枝山的树冠下发现了街道、堤坝和神庙组成的网格。阇耶跋摩后来以吴哥附近的诃里诃罗洲为都，他的继承者们将在那里建起世界上最宏伟的神庙群。

summary.en: King Anawrahta of Pagan took the Mon city of Thaton, carrying its king Manuha, monks, artisans and Pali scriptures back to Pagan. The conquest is remembered as the moment Theravada Buddhism became the religion of the Burmese state.
summary.zh: 蒲甘国王阿奴律陀攻占孟人城市直通，把国王摩奴诃、僧侣、工匠和巴利文三藏带回蒲甘。这次征服被视为上座部佛教成为缅甸国教的开端。

sources.title: Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1829)
Michael Aung-Thwin, The Mists of Rāmañña: The Legend that was Lower Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 2005)
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Wikipedia: Anawrahta

note: 1057 is the chronicle date. Aung-Thwin argues that the Thaton conquest story is a later legend; the QID is the Thaton kingdom, which Wikidata ends in 1057.

story.en:
The Burmese chronicles tell the story as a conversion. A Mon monk from Thaton, Shin Arahan, came to Pagan and so impressed King Anawrahta that the king swept away the old Ari priests and asked Manuha, king of Thaton, for a copy of the Pali scriptures. Manuha refused, and in 1057 Anawrahta marched south and besieged the city.

According to the chronicle, he brought back Manuha and his family, thousands of monks and craftsmen, and the Tipitaka loaded on thirty-two white elephants. Manuha, held captive at Pagan, is said to have built the Manuha temple, whose cramped interior with its huge Buddha images is read as an expression of his confinement.

Modern historians are divided. Michael Aung-Thwin argues that the conquest of Thaton is a legend created centuries later, since no contemporary inscription mentions it. What is clear is that from Anawrahta's reign Pagan became a Theravada kingdom, writing Pali and Mon, and that its kings began the building that left more than two thousand temples on the plain of Bagan.
story.zh:
缅甸编年史把这段历史讲成一次皈依。直通的孟族僧人信阿罗汉来到蒲甘，令阿奴律陀王深为折服；国王废黜了原来的阿利僧，并向直通国王摩奴诃索要巴利文三藏。摩奴诃拒绝了，1057年阿奴律陀挥师南下围攻直通。

据编年史记载，他带回了摩奴诃及其家眷、数千名僧侣和工匠，以及用三十二头白象驮载的三藏经典。被囚于蒲甘的摩奴诃据说建造了摩奴诃寺，寺内空间逼仄而佛像巨大，被解读为他身陷囹圄的心境写照。

现代史学家对此意见分歧。昂杜因认为征服直通是数百年后编造的传说，因为同时代的碑铭对此只字未提。可以确定的是，从阿奴律陀统治时起，蒲甘成为上座部佛教王国，使用巴利文与孟文，历代国王开始兴建佛塔，最终在蒲甘平原上留下了两千多座寺塔。

name.en: Battle of the Như Nguyệt River

summary.en: Song China invaded Đại Việt in 1076–1077 in revenge for Lý Thường Kiệt's raids on Guangxi. Lý Thường Kiệt held the Như Nguyệt (Cầu) river line north of Thăng Long; disease and failed crossings forced the Song to accept peace and withdraw.
summary.zh: 为报复李常杰对广西的袭击，宋朝于1076—1077年入侵大越。李常杰在升龙以北据守如月江（梂江）防线；宋军渡河失败，又遭疫病，被迫议和撤军。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Songshi (History of Song), "Biography of Jiaozhi"
James Anderson, The Rebel Den of Nùng Trí Cao (University of Washington Press, 2007)
Wikipedia: Song–Đại Việt war

story.en:
In late 1075 Lý Thường Kiệt struck first. Hearing that the reformist Song minister Wang Anshi was preparing an invasion, he led an army and fleet into Guangxi, took Qinzhou and Lianzhou and, after a siege of forty-two days, sacked Yongzhou (Nanning) early in 1076, killing much of its population.

The Song counter-attack under Guo Kui reached the Như Nguyệt river, a day's march from Thăng Long, early in 1077. Lý Thường Kiệt had fortified the south bank with palisades. The Song could not get their fleet up the coast to support a crossing, and the attacks that did cross were thrown back. Disease swept the Song camp.

Vietnamese tradition says that one night a voice from the riverside temple recited the poem "Nam quốc sơn hà": the southern country belongs to the southern emperor, as fixed in the book of heaven, and invaders will meet defeat. Its authorship and date are debated, but it is often called Vietnam's first declaration of independence. Guo Kui accepted a truce and withdrew, keeping only a few border districts that were later returned.
story.zh:
1075年末，李常杰先发制人。他听说宋朝变法派宰相王安石正筹划入侵，便率水陆大军攻入广西，夺取钦州、廉州，1076年初又在围城四十二日后攻破邕州（南宁），城中居民死伤甚众。

1077年初，郭逵率宋军反攻，抵达距升龙仅一日路程的如月江。李常杰早已在南岸筑起栅寨。宋军舰队无法沿海北上配合渡江，渡过江的部队又被击退，军营中疫病流行。

越南传说某夜江边神祠中传出诗句：“南国山河南帝居，截然定分在天书，如何逆虏来侵犯，汝等行看取败虚。”这首《南国山河》的作者与年代仍有争议，但常被称为越南第一篇独立宣言。郭逵最终接受议和撤军，只保留了几处边境州县，后来也归还了大越。

summary.en: King Kyansittha's Ananda Temple, a cross-shaped shrine with four standing Buddhas and gilded spires, became the masterpiece of early Pagan architecture. Its corridors hold hundreds of glazed plaques and stone reliefs of the Buddha's lives.
summary.zh: 江喜陀王建造的阿难陀寺呈十字形，内有四尊立佛，塔顶镀金，是蒲甘早期建筑的杰作。寺内回廊镶嵌着数百块釉陶板和佛本生故事石雕。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Bagan
G. H. Luce, Old Burma–Early Pagán (J. J. Augustin, 1969–70)
Wikipedia: Ananda Temple

note: Construction is dated c. 1090–1105; Wikidata gives 1091 as the start.

summary.en: A four-sided stone stele dated 1292, found at Sukhothai in 1833 by the future King Mongkut, praising King Ram Khamhaeng's benevolent rule and claiming that he devised the Thai script. Long a national icon, its authenticity has been debated since the 1980s.
summary.zh: 一块四面刻字的石碑，所署年代为1292年，1833年由后来的蒙固王在素可泰发现。碑文颂扬兰甘亨王的仁政，并称泰文字母由他创制。它长期被视为国宝，但自20世纪80年代起其真伪一直存在争议。

sources.title: A. B. Griswold & Prasert na Nagara, "The Inscription of King Rāma Gamhèn of Sukhodaya (1292 A.D.)", Journal of the Siam Society 59 (1971)
James R. Chamberlain (ed.), The Ram Khamhaeng Controversy (Siam Society, 1991)
UNESCO Memory of the World: The King Ram Khamhaeng Inscription (2003)
Wikipedia: Ram Khamhaeng Inscription

note: Most scholars accept it as 13th-century; Michael Vickery and Piriya Krairiksh argued it was composed in the 19th century.

story.en:
In 1833 the monk-prince Mongkut, on pilgrimage at the ruins of Sukhothai, noticed a stone pillar lying near an old throne. It was covered on four sides in an archaic script. Deciphered, it spoke in the voice of King Ram Khamhaeng: in his time "there are fish in the water and rice in the fields"; the king hung a bell at his palace gate so that any subject with a grievance could ring it; and in 1283 he had invented the Thai letters.

The pillar became the founding text of the Thai nation, taught to every schoolchild and inscribed in 2003 on UNESCO's Memory of the World register. But its very perfection raised doubts. In the 1980s the historian Michael Vickery and the art historian Piriya Krairiksh pointed to spelling, vocabulary and ideas that seemed closer to the 19th century, suggesting Mongkut himself might have composed it to show Siam's ancient civilisation to Western powers.

The debate has not been settled, though most epigraphers now accept a 13th-century date, perhaps with later additions. Either way, the stone shaped how Thais imagine their past.
story.zh:
1833年，出家为僧的王子蒙固在素可泰遗址朝圣时，发现一座古王座旁躺着一根石柱，四面刻满古老的文字。破译后，碑文以兰甘亨王的口吻说：在他统治时“水中有鱼，田里有稻”；国王在宫门挂了一口钟，任何有冤屈的臣民都可以敲响它；1283年他创制了泰文字母。

这根石柱成为泰国的立国文献，每个学童都要学习，2003年还列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》。但它的完美本身引起了怀疑。20世纪80年代，历史学家迈克尔·维克里和艺术史家披利雅·格莱力指出，碑文的拼写、词汇和思想似乎更接近19世纪，暗示可能是蒙固本人为向西方列强展示暹罗的古老文明而撰写的。

这场争论至今没有定论，不过多数碑铭学家现在接受13世纪的年代，或许其中有后人增补。无论如何，这块石碑塑造了泰国人对自身过去的想象。

summary.en: A member of a Yuan embassy, Zhou Daguan lived at Angkor for about a year and wrote "The Customs of Cambodia", the only eyewitness account of the city at its height: its golden towers, royal processions, markets run by women and Chinese settlers.
summary.zh: 元朝使团成员周达观在吴哥居住约一年，写成《真腊风土记》。这是唯一一部亲历吴哥鼎盛时期的记述，描写了金塔、王家仪仗、由妇女经营的集市和当地的华人移民。

sources.title: Zhou Daguan, Zhenla fengtu ji, trans. Peter Harris, A Record of Cambodia: The Land and Its People (Silkworm Books, 2007)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: The Customs of Cambodia

story.en:
In 1296 an embassy sent by Temür Khan, Kublai's successor, sailed from Wenzhou to Cambodia. Among its members was Zhou Daguan, a young man from Zhejiang, who stayed at Angkor from August 1296 to July 1297 and afterwards wrote a short book about what he saw.

He described the walled city of Angkor Thom with a golden tower at its centre (the Bayon), the king riding out on an elephant under white parasols with hundreds of palace women carrying candles, and the bridge lined with stone giants. He noted that trade was the business of women, so Chinese sailors who settled there were quick to take local wives; that slaves were taken from the hill peoples; and that the Cambodians bathed in groups in the rivers several times a day.

His account also hints at strain: the country had recently been devastated by war with the Siamese. Lost for centuries in Chinese collections, the book was translated into French in 1819 and guided the first European explorers of Angkor, and it remains the only description of the city written while it was still living.
story.zh:
1296年，忽必烈的继承者元成宗派遣使团从温州出海前往真腊。使团中有一位来自浙江的年轻人周达观，他于1296年8月至1297年7月留居吴哥，归国后写下一部小书，记录所见所闻。

他描写了城墙环绕的吴哥通王城，城中心有一座金塔（巴戎寺）；国王骑象出巡，张白伞盖，数百宫女手持蜡烛随行；城门石桥两侧排列着石刻巨神。他记载当地贸易由妇女经营，因此在此定居的中国水手很快就娶了当地妻子；奴隶多取自山地民族；当地人每天数次成群到河中洗浴。

他的记述也透露出危机：真腊不久前刚遭暹罗战火蹂躏。这部书在中国典籍中沉寂数百年，1819年被译成法文，引导了最早一批探访吴哥的欧洲人。它至今仍是唯一一部在吴哥尚有生机时写下的城市记录。

summary.en: Mangrai, having conquered Haripunchai and seen his earlier capital at Wiang Kum Kam flood, founded Chiang Mai, the "new city", between Doi Suthep and the Ping river. The chronicle says his allies Ngam Muang of Phayao and Ram Khamhaeng of Sukhothai helped lay it out.
summary.zh: 孟莱王征服哈里奔猜后，因原先的都城温孔岗遭水淹，便在素贴山与滨河之间兴建“新城”清迈。据编年史记载，帕尧的昂孟王和素可泰的兰甘亨王协助他规划了这座城市。

sources.title: David K. Wyatt & Aroonrut Wichienkeeo (trans.), The Chiang Mai Chronicle (Silkworm Books, 2nd ed. 1998)
Hans Penth, A Brief History of Lan Na (Silkworm Books, 1994)
Wikipedia: Chiang Mai

note: The founding date is from the Chiang Mai Chronicle; Wikidata gives a 13th-century inception.

name.zh: 加查·马达的帕拉帕誓言

summary.en: On becoming chief minister of Majapahit, Gajah Mada swore, according to the Pararaton, that he would taste no palapa (spice, or pleasure) until he had united the islands of the archipelago under Majapahit. Modern Indonesia adopted the oath as a symbol of national unity.
summary.zh: 据《诸王志》记载，加查·马达出任满者伯夷宰相时发誓：在把群岛诸岛统一于满者伯夷之前，绝不享用“帕拉帕”（香料，或享乐）。现代印尼把这一誓言当作民族统一的象征。

sources.title: Pararaton (Book of Kings), Old Javanese chronicle
Theodore G. Th. Pigeaud, Java in the 14th Century: A Study in Cultural History (Martinus Nijhoff, 1960–63)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Palapa oath

note: Known only from the later Pararaton; the meaning of "palapa" is uncertain. Indonesia named its first communications satellite Palapa (1976).

summary.en: The Sundanese king came to Majapahit to marry his daughter Dyah Pitaloka to Hayam Wuruk. Gajah Mada demanded that she be handed over as a token of submission; the Sundanese royal party fought and was killed to a man at the Bubat field, and the princess is said to have taken her life.
summary.zh: 巽他国王带着女儿迪亚·毗塔洛卡前往满者伯夷与哈亚·乌鲁克成婚。加查·马达要求把公主作为臣服的贡品献上，巽他王室随员奋起抵抗，在布巴特广场全数战死，据说公主也随之自尽。

sources.title: Pararaton (Book of Kings), Old Javanese chronicle
Kidung Sunda (Middle Javanese poem)
Theodore G. Th. Pigeaud, Java in the 14th Century: A Study in Cultural History (Martinus Nijhoff, 1960–63)
Wikipedia: Battle of Bubat

note: Known from the Pararaton and the Kidung Sunda, not from the Nagarakretagama; the event soured Javanese–Sundanese relations for centuries.
