summary.en: Prince U Thong, possibly of a Chinese merchant family, moved his court to an island in the Chao Phraya, perhaps fleeing epidemic, and was crowned Ramathibodi I. Ayutthaya soon absorbed Sukhothai, sacked Angkor and became the main power of mainland Southeast Asia.
summary.zh: 可能出身华商家族的乌通王子，或许为躲避瘟疫，将王廷迁到湄南河中的一座岛上，加冕为拉玛铁菩提一世。阿瑜陀耶很快吞并素可泰、攻陷吴哥，成为东南亚大陆的主要强国。

sources.title: Royal Chronicles of Ayutthaya (Luang Prasoet version)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Ayutthaya (Cambridge University Press, 2017)
Wikipedia: Ayutthaya Kingdom

note: The date is from the Luang Prasoet chronicle; a settlement existed on the site earlier.

summary.en: Returning from exile at Angkor with a Khmer army, Fa Ngum subdued the Lao principalities of the middle Mekong and was crowned at Xieng Dong Xieng Thong (Luang Prabang), founding Lan Xang, the "million elephants" kingdom that is the ancestor of Laos.
summary.zh: 法昂率高棉军队从吴哥流亡归来，征服湄公河中游的老族诸邦，在川铜（琅勃拉邦）加冕，建立“百万大象”澜沧王国，即老挝的前身。

sources.title: Martin Stuart-Fox, The Lao Kingdom of Lān Xāng: Rise and Decline (White Lotus, 1998)
Nithan Khun Borom (Lao chronicle)
Wikipedia: Lan Xang

note: The date is traditional (some sources 1354); Wikidata's coordinate is a country centroid.

name.zh: 大越攻陷毗阇耶（阇槃城）

summary.en: Lê Thánh Tông led a vast army south and stormed Vijaya (Chà Bàn), the Cham capital near Quy Nhơn, killing and capturing tens of thousands and taking King Trà Toàn prisoner. Champa never recovered; its rump states survived further south until the 19th century.
summary.zh: 黎圣宗率大军南下，攻破归仁附近的占城都城毗阇耶（阇槃），杀死和俘获数万人，生擒国王槃罗茶全。占城从此一蹶不振，残余小邦在更南方苟延至19世纪。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Ming shilu (Veritable Records of the Ming), Chenghua reign
Wikipedia: Champa–Đại Việt War (1471)

note: Casualty figures come from the Vietnamese annals and may be inflated.

story.en:
By the 1460s Champa had fought Đại Việt on and off for five centuries, and in 1470 its king Trà Toàn attacked the Vietnamese frontier garrisons. Lê Thánh Tông answered with the largest army the country had ever raised: the annals speak of 260,000 men and a war fleet that sailed down the coast.

In March 1471 the Vietnamese reached Vijaya, the Cham capital on the plain behind Quy Nhơn. After a siege of a few days it fell. The annals record 40,000 killed and 30,000 captured, among them Trà Toàn and fifty members of the royal family; the king died on the voyage north. Lê Thánh Tông annexed the land as far as the Cù Mông pass and set up the province of Quảng Nam, and he divided the remaining Cham territory into small client states.

The Ming court, to which both kingdoms sent tribute, protested but did nothing. The fall of Vijaya ended Champa as a regional power and opened the long Vietnamese "march to the south" that reached the Mekong delta three centuries later.
story.zh:
到15世纪60年代，占城与大越断断续续交战已有五个世纪。1470年占城国王槃罗茶全进攻大越边防。黎圣宗以越南有史以来最庞大的军队回应：史书称有二十六万人，另有战船沿海南下。

1471年3月，大越军抵达归仁平原后方的占城都城毗阇耶，围城数日即破。据越南史书记载，杀四万人、俘三万人，其中包括槃罗茶全和五十名王族成员，国王在押往北方的途中死去。黎圣宗将直到瞿蒙关的土地并入版图，设广南道，又把剩下的占城领土分为几个附属小国。

两国都向明朝朝贡，明廷虽提出抗议却未采取行动。毗阇耶的陷落终结了占城作为地区强国的地位，开启了越南漫长的“南进”，三个世纪后一直推进到湄公河三角洲。

summary.en: During the fourth Burmese invasion of Ayutthaya, King Naresuan met the Burmese crown prince Mingyi Swa near Suphan Buri. Thai chronicles say Naresuan killed him in single combat on war elephants; the invasion collapsed and Siam stayed free of Burmese overlordship.
summary.zh: 缅甸第四次入侵阿瑜陀耶时，纳黎萱王在素攀武里附近与缅甸王储明吉斯瓦相遇。泰国编年史称纳黎萱在战象对决中将其斩杀；缅军入侵随即瓦解，暹罗从此摆脱缅甸的宗主权。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Ayutthaya (Cambridge University Press, 2017)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1829)
Wikipedia: Battle of Nong Sarai

note: Thai and Burmese chronicles give different accounts and dates (the Thai date 18 January 1593 is commemorated as Royal Thai Armed Forces Day). Burmese sources say Mingyi Swa was shot; Terwiel (2013) doubts that a formal elephant duel took place.

name.en: Dutch conquest of the Banda Islands
name.zh: 荷兰征服班达群岛（班达大屠杀）

summary.en: To secure a monopoly of nutmeg and mace, Jan Pieterszoon Coen invaded the Banda Islands with VOC troops and Japanese mercenaries. Thousands of Bandanese were killed, starved or enslaved and deported; the islands were resettled with Dutch planters working imported slaves.
summary.zh: 为垄断肉豆蔻与肉豆蔻衣，扬·彼得生·库恩率荷兰东印度公司军队和日本雇佣兵入侵班达群岛。数千班达人被杀、饿死或沦为奴隶遭流放，群岛随后由荷兰种植园主带着输入的奴隶重新占据。

sources.title: Vincent C. Loth, "Armed Incidents and Unpaid Bills: Anglo-Dutch Rivalry in the Banda Islands", Modern Asian Studies 29 (1995)
Willard A. Hanna, Indonesian Banda: Colonialism and its Aftermath in the Nutmeg Islands (ISHI, 1978)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Dutch conquest of the Banda Islands

note: The pre-conquest population (often put at about 15,000) and the numbers killed are estimates; the Dutch figures were 2,800 killed and 1,700 enslaved.

story.en:
In the early 17th century the Banda Islands, a speck of volcanic islands in the Banda Sea, were the only place on earth where nutmeg grew. Their elected elders, the orang kaya, sold to Javanese, Malay, English and Dutch buyers alike, and broke the exclusive contracts the Dutch pressed on them.

Jan Pieterszoon Coen, governor-general of the VOC, decided to end the problem by force. In early 1621 he landed on Lonthor with about two thousand men, including Japanese mercenaries. Villages were burned, and many Bandanese fled to the mountains, where they died of hunger, or jumped from cliffs rather than surrender. Accused of conspiracy, some forty orang kaya were tortured and then beheaded and quartered by the Japanese soldiers inside a bamboo enclosure; a Dutch officer who witnessed it recorded his horror.

Within a few years only a fraction of the population remained on the islands. Survivors were shipped to Batavia as slaves or escaped to the Kei islands, whose villages still speak Bandanese. The VOC divided the nutmeg groves into perken worked by slaves under Dutch perkeniers, a system that lasted two centuries. Even the Heeren XVII in Amsterdam rebuked Coen for his methods.
story.zh:
17世纪初，班达海中星点般的火山小岛班达群岛是世界上唯一出产肉豆蔻的地方。岛上推举的长老“奥朗卡亚”同时向爪哇、马来、英国和荷兰商人出售香料，屡次违背荷兰人强加的独家合约。

荷兰东印度公司总督扬·彼得生·库恩决定用武力解决问题。1621年初，他率约两千人（包括日本雇佣兵）登陆伦托尔岛。村庄被焚毁，许多班达人逃进山中饿死，或宁愿跳崖也不投降。约四十名奥朗卡亚被控谋反，遭受酷刑后在一个竹围栏内被日本兵斩首分尸；在场的一名荷兰军官记下了自己的惊恐。

几年之内，岛上只剩下原有人口的一小部分。幸存者被作为奴隶运往巴达维亚，或逃到凯伊群岛，那里的村庄至今仍讲班达语。公司把肉豆蔻林分成若干“园地”，由荷兰园主驱使奴隶耕作，这一制度延续了两个世纪。就连阿姆斯特丹的十七人董事会也谴责了库恩的手段。

name.zh: 苏丹阿贡围攻巴达维亚

summary.en: Sultan Agung of Mataram twice sent armies across Java to drive the VOC from Batavia. Both sieges failed; in 1629 Dutch ships burned the rice stores Mataram had stockpiled at Tegal and Cirebon, and the besiegers starved. Coen died of disease inside the town.
summary.zh: 马打兰苏丹阿贡两次派大军横越爪哇，试图把荷兰东印度公司赶出巴达维亚，均告失败。1629年荷兰船只焚毁了马打兰囤积在直葛和井里汶的粮仓，围城军队陷入饥荒。库恩在城中病逝。

label.zh: 第二次围攻巴达维亚失败

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
H. J. de Graaf, De regering van Sultan Agung (Nijhoff, 1958)
Wikipedia: Siege of Batavia

note: Wikidata's coordinate lies in Central Java; the point here is Batavia itself.

story.en:
By the 1620s Sultan Agung ruled almost all of Java except two places: the old port of Banten and the Dutch fort at Batavia, which he regarded as an upstart vassal that refused to pay homage. In August 1628 his fleet and army appeared before the town. Mataram's troops dug trenches and tried to dam the river to flood the walls, but the Dutch held, and by December the attackers withdrew. Agung is said to have executed the commanders who failed him.

The second campaign, in 1629, was planned more carefully, with rice depots along the north coast to feed tens of thousands of soldiers. The VOC learned of them, and its ships sailed along the coast burning the barns at Tegal and Cirebon. When the Javanese army arrived, it was already hungry, and the siege collapsed in disease and starvation.

Inside Batavia, Coen died in September 1629, probably of dysentery. Agung never again attacked the Dutch, and their fort survived to become the capital of an empire that would eventually swallow Mataram itself.
story.zh:
到17世纪20年代，苏丹阿贡几乎统治了整个爪哇，只剩两处例外：老港万丹和荷兰人在巴达维亚的城堡。在他看来，后者是个拒不朝贡的暴发户藩属。1628年8月，他的舰队和大军兵临城下。马打兰军队挖掘壕沟，并试图筑坝引河水淹城墙，但荷兰人坚守不退，到12月进攻者撤兵。据说阿贡处死了作战不力的将领。

1629年的第二次远征准备更加周密，沿北海岸设立了粮站，以供给数万士兵。荷兰东印度公司得知后，派船沿海岸焚毁了直葛和井里汶的粮仓。爪哇军队抵达时已经饥肠辘辘，围城最终在疫病和饥饿中瓦解。

城内的库恩于1629年9月去世，很可能死于痢疾。阿贡此后再未进攻荷兰人，而这座城堡存续下来，成为一个最终吞并马打兰本身的帝国的首都。

summary.en: A VOC fleet allied with the Sultanate of Johor besieged Portuguese Malacca for more than five months. Famine and disease killed most of the defenders and townspeople before the Dutch stormed the fortress on 14 January 1641, ending 130 years of Portuguese rule.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司舰队与柔佛苏丹国联手围攻葡属马六甲五个多月。守军和居民大多死于饥荒和疫病，1641年1月14日荷兰人攻破要塞，结束了葡萄牙130年的统治。

sources.title: Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
C. R. Boxer, The Dutch Seaborne Empire 1600–1800 (Hutchinson, 1965)
Wikipedia: Siege of Malacca (1640–1641)

summary.en: Two clans ruling in the name of the powerless Lê emperors fought seven campaigns across the Gianh river: the Trịnh in the north (Đàng Ngoài) and the Nguyễn in the south (Đàng Trong). Nguyễn walls at Đồng Hới, armed with Portuguese-made cannon, held; the truce of 1672 split Vietnam for a century.
summary.zh: 以傀儡黎帝名义执政的两大家族隔灵江七次交战：北方（塘外）的郑主与南方（塘中）的阮主。阮主在洞海修筑的长垒配备葡萄牙大炮，屡挡郑军；1672年停战后越南南北分治长达一个世纪。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Li Tana, Nguyễn Cochinchina: Southern Vietnam in the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries (Cornell SEAP, 1998)
Wikipedia: Trịnh–Nguyễn War

summary.en: The VOC admiral Cornelis Speelman, allied with the Bugis prince Arung Palakka of Bone, attacked the Gowa sultanate, the great free port of eastern Indonesia. Sultan Hasanuddin signed the Treaty of Bongaya in 1667; when fighting resumed, the fortress of Somba Opu fell in June 1669.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司将领斯皮尔曼与骨部的布吉斯王子阿隆·帕拉卡结盟，进攻印尼东部最大的自由港戈瓦苏丹国。哈桑努丁苏丹于1667年签订《本加亚条约》；战事再起后，松巴奥普要塞于1669年6月陷落。

sources.title: Leonard Y. Andaya, The Heritage of Arung Palakka (Martinus Nijhoff, 1981)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Makassar War

name.zh: 红溪惨案（1740年巴达维亚大屠杀）

summary.en: Amid rumours of a Chinese uprising, VOC soldiers and townspeople killed some 10,000 ethnic Chinese in Batavia over two weeks in October 1740. The Chinese quarter burned, survivors joined Javanese rebels in a war that spread along the coast, and Governor-General Valckenier was recalled and imprisoned.
summary.zh: 在华人起事的谣言中，1740年10月荷兰东印度公司士兵和市民在两周内杀害了巴达维亚约一万名华人。华人区被焚，幸存者与爪哇起义者联合，战火沿海岸蔓延；总督瓦尔肯尼尔被召回并遭监禁。

sources.title: Leonard Blussé, Strange Company: Chinese Settlers, Mestizo Women and the Dutch in VOC Batavia (Foris, 1986)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: 1740 Batavia massacre

story.en:
Batavia depended on its Chinese: they milled its sugar, built its houses, collected its taxes and ran its shops. By the 1730s, however, the sugar trade had slumped, unemployed Chinese labourers filled the countryside, and the VOC began deporting "surplus" Chinese to Ceylon. A rumour spread that the deportees were being thrown overboard at sea.

In early October 1740 bands of Chinese attacked VOC posts outside the walls. Inside the city, Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier's council ordered a curfew and house searches. On 9 October fires broke out in the Chinese quarter, and soldiers, sailors and townspeople, among them many slaves, began to kill. Patients in the hospital and prisoners in the jail were murdered. Over the following days some 10,000 people died, and the Kali Angke canal is said to have run red, which is why Chinese call the event Hongxi, the "Red River".

Survivors fled east and joined forces with Javanese rebels in the "China War" that engulfed the north coast and led to the division of Mataram. In Amsterdam the directors recalled Valckenier, who died in prison in Batavia in 1751 before his trial ended.
story.zh:
巴达维亚离不开华人：他们经营糖厂、建造房屋、包收税款、开设店铺。然而到18世纪30年代，糖业衰退，失业的华人劳工遍布城郊，荷兰东印度公司开始把“多余”的华人遣送锡兰。随即有谣言说，被遣送者在海上被扔下船。

1740年10月初，成群的华人袭击了城外的公司哨所。城内，总督阿德里安·瓦尔肯尼尔的议会下令宵禁和搜查民宅。10月9日，华人区燃起大火，士兵、水手和市民（其中有许多奴隶）开始杀戮，医院里的病人和监狱中的囚犯也惨遭杀害。此后数日约有一万人罹难，据说安格克河被鲜血染红，华人因此称之为“红溪惨案”。

幸存者向东逃亡，与爪哇起义者联合，掀起席卷北海岸的“华人战争”，并导致马打兰的分裂。阿姆斯特丹的董事会召回了瓦尔肯尼尔，他在审判结束前于1751年死于巴达维亚的狱中。

note: Death toll estimates range from about 5,000 to more than 10,000; 10,000 is the figure most often given.

summary.en: Three brothers from Tây Sơn village in Bình Định led a rebellion against the Nguyễn lords' taxes in 1771 that grew into a thirty-year civil war. They overthrew the Nguyễn, Trịnh and Lê, defeated Siamese and Qing armies, and were finally destroyed by the surviving Nguyễn prince, Nguyễn Ánh.
summary.zh: 1771年，平定西山邑的三兄弟因不堪阮主苛税而起事，演变为长达三十年的内战。他们先后推翻阮主、郑主和后黎朝，击败暹罗与清朝军队，最终被阮氏遗孤阮福映所灭。

label.en: Gia Định taken; Nguyễn lords killed
Siamese routed at Rạch Gầm–Xoài Mút
Nguyễn Ánh, in Phú Xuân since 1801, takes the north
label.zh: 阮福映（1801年已取富春）攻取北方

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
George Dutton, The Tây Sơn Uprising (University of Hawaii Press, 2006)
Wikipedia: Tây Sơn wars

name.en: Gia Long founds the Nguyễn dynasty

summary.en: Having defeated the Tây Sơn, Nguyễn Phúc Ánh proclaimed the Gia Long reign at Phú Xuân (Huế) and, for the first time, ruled a Vietnam stretching from the Chinese border to the Gulf of Thailand. In 1804 the Qing recognised the country as Việt Nam.
summary.zh: 击败西山朝后，阮福映在富春（顺化）改元嘉隆，首次统治北起中国边界、南至暹罗湾的完整越南。1804年清朝册封其国号为“越南”。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Alexander Woodside, Vietnam and the Chinese Model (Harvard University Press, 1971)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Complex of Huế Monuments
Wikipedia: Nguyễn dynasty

name.zh: 莱佛士建立英属新加坡

summary.en: Stamford Raffles and William Farquhar landed at the Singapore river in January 1819 and, by recognising Tengku Hussein as Sultan of Johor, won the right to set up an East India Company trading post. As a free port it grew within five years into the busiest entrepôt of the Straits.
summary.zh: 1819年1月，斯坦福·莱佛士和威廉·法夸尔在新加坡河口登陆，通过承认东姑胡先为柔佛苏丹，取得了设立东印度公司贸易站的权利。作为自由港，它在五年内成为马六甲海峡最繁忙的转口港。

sources.title: C. M. Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore 1819–2005 (NUS Press, 2009)
John N. Miksic, Singapore and the Silk Road of the Sea, 1300–1800 (NUS Press, 2013)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Singapore: History
Wikipedia: Founding of modern Singapore

story.en:
After the Napoleonic Wars Britain handed Java back to the Netherlands, and the Dutch moved to close the Straits of Malacca to British ships. Stamford Raffles, then lieutenant-governor of Bencoolen in Sumatra, persuaded the governor-general in Calcutta to let him find a new station at the southern end of the Straits.

On 28 January 1819 his ships anchored off the mouth of the Singapore river, where a few hundred Malays and Orang Laut lived under the Temenggong of Johor. Johor's throne was disputed, and the Dutch backed the younger brother. Raffles brought the elder, Tengku Hussein, over from the Riau islands, recognised him as sultan, and on 6 February signed a treaty with him and the Temenggong allowing the Company to build a factory in return for annual payments.

Raffles stayed only a few days, leaving William Farquhar in charge. He declared the port free of duties, and Chinese, Bugis, Arab and Indian traders poured in. The Dutch protested, but the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 left Singapore in British hands.
story.zh:
拿破仑战争结束后，英国把爪哇归还荷兰，荷兰随即试图对英国船只封锁马六甲海峡。时任苏门答腊明古鲁副总督的斯坦福·莱佛士说服加尔各答的总督，准许他在海峡南端另觅据点。

1819年1月28日，他的船队停泊在新加坡河口，那里有数百名马来人和海人，受柔佛天猛公管辖。柔佛王位当时存在争议，荷兰支持弟弟一方。莱佛士从廖内群岛接来哥哥东姑胡先，承认他为苏丹，并于2月6日与他和天猛公签约：公司可在此建立商馆，作为回报每年付给二人款项。

莱佛士只停留了几天，便把事务交给威廉·法夸尔。他宣布新加坡为免税的自由港，华人、布吉斯人、阿拉伯人和印度商人蜂拥而至。荷兰提出抗议，但1824年的《英荷条约》确认新加坡归英国所有。

summary.en: Border clashes over Arakan, Manipur and Assam led British India to invade Burma by sea. After Rangoon fell, disease killed far more British troops than battle, but General Bandula was killed at Danubyu and the Treaty of Yandabo (1826) cost Burma its western provinces and a huge indemnity.
summary.zh: 因阿拉干、曼尼普尔和阿萨姆的边境冲突，英属印度从海路入侵缅甸。仰光陷落后，英军死于疾病者远多于战死者，但缅军名将班都拉在达努彪阵亡，1826年的《杨达波条约》使缅甸失去西部诸省并支付巨额赔款。

sources.title: Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Wikipedia: First Anglo-Burmese War

summary.en: Signed in London, the treaty divided the Malay world along the Straits of Malacca: Britain gave up Bencoolen in Sumatra, the Netherlands gave up Malacca and its objections to Singapore. The line it drew became, in effect, the border between Malaysia and Indonesia.
summary.zh: 该条约在伦敦签订，沿马六甲海峡瓜分马来世界：英国放弃苏门答腊的明古鲁，荷兰放弃马六甲并不再反对英国占有新加坡。条约划出的界线实际上成为后来马来西亚与印度尼西亚的边界。

sources.title: Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Nicholas Tarling, Anglo-Dutch Rivalry in the Malay World, 1780–1824 (Cambridge University Press, 1962)
Wikipedia: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824

note: Signed in London; the point marks the Strait of Malacca, where its line was drawn.

summary.en: Governor-General Van den Bosch required Javanese villages to grow export crops, above all coffee, sugar and indigo, on a share of their land or to work for the government. The profits rescued the Dutch treasury, while forced cropping contributed to famines in Cirebon and Central Java in the 1840s.
summary.zh: 总督范登博斯规定爪哇村庄须拿出部分土地种植咖啡、甘蔗、靛蓝等出口作物，或为政府服劳役。所得利润挽救了荷兰国库，而强迫种植则加剧了19世纪40年代井里汶和中爪哇的饥荒。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Robert E. Elson, Village Java under the Cultivation System, 1830–1870 (Allen & Unwin, 1994)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Culture System
Wikipedia: Cultivation System

note: Point placed in Central Java; the system covered most of Java.

summary.en: King Mongkut signed a treaty with Britain's envoy John Bowring fixing import duties at 3 per cent, ending royal trade monopolies and granting British subjects extraterritoriality. It opened Siam to free trade and rice exports, and similar treaties with other powers followed.
summary.zh: 蒙固王与英国使节约翰·宝宁签订条约，将进口关税定为3%，取消王室贸易专营，并给予英国臣民治外法权。条约使暹罗向自由贸易和大米出口开放，其他列强随后订立了类似条约。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
John Bowring, The Kingdom and People of Siam (London, 1857)
Wikipedia: Bowring Treaty

summary.en: Over eight years the naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace collected some 125,000 specimens across the archipelago. On Ternate in 1858 he wrote the essay on natural selection that prompted Darwin to publish, and he noticed the sharp faunal boundary between Bali and Lombok now called the Wallace Line.
summary.zh: 博物学家阿尔弗雷德·拉塞尔·华莱士用八年时间在马来群岛采集了约十二万五千件标本。1858年他在特尔纳特写下关于自然选择的论文，促使达尔文发表其理论；他还注意到巴厘岛与龙目岛之间动物分布的明显界线，即今天所称的“华莱士线”。

sources.title: Alfred Russel Wallace, The Malay Archipelago (Macmillan, 1869)
Natural History Museum, London: Alfred Russel Wallace
Wikipedia: Wallace Line

note: Point placed on the Lombok Strait, where the line runs.

name.en: Siege of Tourane: French conquest begins
name.zh: 土伦之围：法国征服越南的开端

summary.en: Citing the persecution of Catholic missionaries, a Franco-Spanish fleet under Admiral Rigault de Genouilly seized Tourane (Đà Nẵng) in September 1858. Disease pinned the force down, so it turned south and took Saigon in 1859; by the treaty of 1862 Emperor Tự Đức ceded three provinces of Cochinchina.
summary.zh: 以天主教传教士遭迫害为由，里戈·德·热努伊率领的法西联合舰队于1858年9月攻占土伦（岘港）。疫病使远征军困守不前，于是转而南下，1859年攻占西贡；根据1862年条约，嗣德帝割让交趾支那东部三省。

sources.title: Pierre Brocheux & Daniel Hémery, Indochina: An Ambiguous Colonization, 1858–1954 (University of California Press, 2009)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Siege of Tourane

name.zh: 穆尔塔图里出版《马格斯·哈弗拉尔》

summary.en: Eduard Douwes Dekker, a former colonial official in Lebak, published under the pen name Multatuli a novel exposing the extortion of Javanese peasants by native chiefs and the Dutch authorities. It shocked Dutch readers and fed the campaign against the Cultivation System.
summary.zh: 曾在勒巴克任殖民官员的爱德华·道韦斯·德克尔以“穆尔塔图里”为笔名出版小说，揭露当地头人和荷兰当局对爪哇农民的盘剥。小说震动了荷兰读者，推动了反对强迫种植制度的运动。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Max Havelaar
Wikipedia: Max Havelaar

note: Point placed at Rangkasbitung, Lebak, where the story is set.

summary.en: The Netherlands invaded the Aceh Sultanate to stop it courting foreign powers. After the first expedition's commander was killed, a long guerrilla war led by ulama and nobles such as Teuku Umar and Cut Nyak Dhien followed; General van Heutsz's mobile columns broke organised resistance by 1904.
summary.zh: 荷兰为阻止亚齐苏丹国结交外国势力而发动入侵。首次远征的司令阵亡后，乌理玛和贵族（如特乌库·乌马尔和朱月婷）领导了旷日持久的游击战；范赫茨将军的机动纵队到1904年瓦解了有组织的抵抗。

sources.title: Anthony Reid, The Contest for North Sumatra (Oxford University Press, 1969)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Aceh War
Wikipedia: Aceh War

note: Point at Kutaraja (Banda Aceh), where the war began; Wikidata's point is in central Aceh.

story.en:
In April 1873 a Dutch expedition landed near Kutaraja, the Acehnese capital, expecting a quick campaign. Within days its commander, General Köhler, was shot dead near the great mosque, and the troops withdrew. A second, larger force took the sultan's palace in 1874, and the Dutch declared the war won.

It had barely begun. The ulama preached holy war, and resistance passed from the court to village leaders. Teuku Umar famously changed sides in 1893, took Dutch arms and money and then deserted with them in 1896. His wife Cut Nyak Dhien fought on after his death, leading a dwindling band through the forests until she was betrayed in 1905.

The Dutch Islam scholar Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje, who had studied in Mecca, advised separating the uleebalang nobility from the ulama and crushing the latter. General J. B. van Heutsz put this into practice with small, mobile marechaussee units, and by 1904 the war was officially over, though killings continued for years. Tens of thousands of Acehnese and some 37,000 colonial soldiers and labourers died.
story.zh:
1873年4月，荷兰远征军在亚齐首都哥打拉惹附近登陆，本以为能速战速决。没过几天，司令克勒将军就在大清真寺附近中弹身亡，部队随即撤退。1874年，第二支规模更大的部队攻占了苏丹王宫，荷兰人宣布战争胜利。

其实战争才刚刚开始。乌理玛号召圣战，抵抗的重心从宫廷转向乡村首领。特乌库·乌马尔于1893年倒向荷兰，拿到武器和钱财后，1896年又带着它们倒戈而去，此事广为人知。他死后，妻子朱月婷继续作战，率领日渐稀少的部众在森林中辗转，直到1905年被人出卖。

曾在麦加求学的荷兰伊斯兰学者斯努克·许尔赫罗涅建议把贵族阶层与乌理玛分化开来，集中打击后者。范赫茨将军以小规模机动的宪兵队付诸实施，到1904年战争正式结束，但杀戮又持续了多年。数万名亚齐人以及约三万七千名殖民军士兵和劳工在战争中死去。

name.en: Third Anglo-Burmese War and the fall of Mandalay
name.zh: 第三次英缅战争与曼德勒陷落

summary.en: Using a timber company's dispute and fears of French influence as pretexts, British steamers carried an army up the Irrawaddy and took Mandalay within three weeks. King Thibaw and Queen Supayalat were exiled to Ratnagiri in India, and Upper Burma was annexed on 1 January 1886.
summary.zh: 英国以一家木材公司的纠纷和担心法国势力渗透为借口，用汽船沿伊洛瓦底江运兵北上，三周内攻占曼德勒。锡袍王和素帕雅叻王后被流放到印度拉特纳吉里，上缅甸于1886年1月1日被吞并。

sources.title: Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
Thant Myint-U, The Making of Modern Burma (Cambridge University Press, 2001)
Wikipedia: Third Anglo-Burmese War

note: Mandalay fell on 28 November 1885; guerrilla resistance lasted into the 1890s.

summary.en: France joined Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia into the Indochinese Union under one governor-general; Laos, a French protectorate from 1893, was formally added in 1899. The federation lasted until the defeat at Điện Biên Phủ.
summary.zh: 法国将交趾支那、安南、东京和柬埔寨合并为印度支那联邦，由一名总督统辖；1893年成为法国保护国的老挝于1899年正式并入。这一联邦一直维持到奠边府战败。

sources.title: Pierre Brocheux & Daniel Hémery, Indochina: An Ambiguous Colonization, 1858–1954 (University of California Press, 2009)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: French Indochina
Wikipedia: French Indochina

summary.en: The Dutch army doctor Eugène Dubois, searching for a "missing link", dug up a skullcap and later a thigh bone on the Solo river at Trinil. He named the species Pithecanthropus erectus; now classed as Homo erectus, it was the first fossil of that species ever found.
summary.zh: 荷兰军医欧仁·杜布瓦为寻找“缺失的环节”，在特里尼尔的梭罗河畔挖出一块头盖骨，后来又发现一根股骨。他将其命名为“直立猿人”，现归入直立人，是该物种最早被发现的化石。

sources.title: Pat Shipman, The Man Who Found the Missing Link: Eugène Dubois (Simon & Schuster, 2001)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Java man
Wikipedia: Java Man

summary.en: Two French gunboats forced their way past the Siamese forts at Paknam and anchored off Bangkok's palace. Under blockade, King Chulalongkorn ceded the left bank of the Mekong, most of today's Laos, to France, a humiliation that spurred his reforms.
summary.zh: 两艘法国炮舰强行闯过北榄的暹罗炮台，停泊在曼谷王宫对面。在封锁之下，朱拉隆功国王将湄公河左岸（今老挝大部）割让给法国。这一屈辱促使他加快改革。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Franco-Siamese crisis of 1893

summary.en: From a window of his house in Kawit, Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed the independence of the Philippines from Spain; the national flag was unfurled and the national anthem played for the first time. Neither Spain nor the United States recognised it.
summary.zh: 埃米利奥·阿奎纳多在卡维特自家宅邸的窗前宣布菲律宾脱离西班牙独立，国旗首次升起，国歌首次奏响。西班牙和美国都不承认这一宣言。

sources.title: Teodoro A. Agoncillo, History of the Filipino People (8th ed., Garotech, 1990)
National Historical Commission of the Philippines: Aguinaldo Shrine
Wikipedia: Philippine Declaration of Independence

summary.en: After buying the Philippines from Spain, the United States fought the First Philippine Republic. Aguinaldo's army turned to guerrilla war; US forces used reconcentration and the "water cure". Some 4,200 Americans and 20,000 Filipino soldiers died, and perhaps 200,000 or more civilians, mostly from disease and famine.
summary.zh: 美国从西班牙手中购得菲律宾后，与第一菲律宾共和国开战。阿奎纳多的军队转入游击战，美军则采取集中营和“水刑”。约4200名美军和2万名菲律宾士兵死亡，平民死亡人数可能达20万甚至更多，大多死于疾病和饥荒。

label.en: Shots at San Juan bridge, Manila

label.zh: 阿奎纳多在帕拉南被俘（3月）

label.en: Balangiga attack and reprisals in Samar (September)
label.zh: 巴兰吉加袭击与萨马岛报复（9月）

sources.title: Brian McAllister Linn, The Philippine War, 1899–1902 (University Press of Kansas, 2000)
US Department of State, Office of the Historian: The Philippine-American War, 1899–1902
Teodoro A. Agoncillo, History of the Filipino People (8th ed., Garotech, 1990)
Wikipedia: Philippine–American War

note: Civilian death estimates range from about 200,000 to much higher; fighting in the Muslim south continued until 1913.

story.en:
By the Treaty of Paris of December 1898 Spain sold the Philippines to the United States for 20 million dollars. Filipinos who had proclaimed their own republic at Malolos refused to be transferred. On the night of 4 February 1899 an American sentry fired on Filipino soldiers near the San Juan bridge in Manila, and the war began.

In open battle the Filipino army was no match for the Americans, and by late 1899 Aguinaldo had dispersed it into guerrilla bands. The war turned brutal. After guerrillas killed 48 American soldiers at Balangiga, Samar, in September 1901, General Jacob Smith ordered the island turned into a "howling wilderness" and told his men to kill everyone over ten. In Batangas whole populations were herded into reconcentration zones where cholera and hunger killed thousands.

Aguinaldo was captured in March 1901 by Frederick Funston, whose men posed as prisoners of Macabebe scouts, and he called on Filipinos to accept American rule. President Theodore Roosevelt declared the war over on 4 July 1902. In the United States the war split opinion: Mark Twain and the Anti-Imperialist League denounced it, and Senate hearings exposed the use of torture.
story.zh:
根据1898年12月的《巴黎条约》，西班牙以两千万美元把菲律宾卖给美国。已在马洛洛斯宣布成立共和国的菲律宾人拒绝被转手。1899年2月4日夜，一名美国哨兵在马尼拉圣胡安桥附近向菲律宾士兵开枪，战争由此爆发。

在正面作战中，菲律宾军队远非美军对手，到1899年底阿奎纳多把部队化整为零，转入游击战。战争随之变得残酷。1901年9月，游击队在萨马岛巴兰吉加杀死48名美军士兵，雅各布·史密斯将军下令把全岛变成“哀号的荒野”，要部下杀死所有十岁以上的人。在八打雁，整村居民被驱入集中区，数以千计的人死于霍乱和饥饿。

1901年3月，弗雷德里克·芬斯顿让部下假扮马卡贝贝侦察兵押送的俘虏，俘获了阿奎纳多；阿奎纳多随后呼吁菲律宾人接受美国统治。1902年7月4日，西奥多·罗斯福总统宣布战争结束。这场战争在美国国内引发分裂：马克·吐温和反帝国主义联盟予以谴责，参议院听证会也揭露了酷刑的使用。

summary.en: At the Second Youth Congress in Batavia, students from Java, Sumatra, Sulawesi, Ambon and elsewhere pledged loyalty to one motherland, one nation and one language, Indonesia. W. R. Supratman played "Indonesia Raya", the future national anthem, on the violin.
summary.zh: 在巴达维亚召开的第二次青年代表大会上，来自爪哇、苏门答腊、苏拉威西、安汶等地的学生宣誓：一个祖国、一个民族、一种语言——印度尼西亚。苏普拉特曼用小提琴演奏了后来成为国歌的《伟大的印度尼西亚》。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Keith Foulcher, "Sumpah Pemuda: The Making and Meaning of a Symbol of Indonesian Nationhood", Asian Studies Review 24 (2000)
Wikipedia: Youth Pledge

summary.en: Japanese troops who had raced down the Malay Peninsula crossed the Johor Strait on 8 February 1942; a week later General Percival surrendered about 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops to General Yamashita. Churchill called it the worst disaster in British military history; the Sook Ching massacres of Chinese followed.
summary.zh: 日军沿马来半岛疾速南下，1942年2月8日渡过柔佛海峡；一周后白思华将军率约八万名英国、印度和澳大利亚官兵向山下奉文投降。丘吉尔称之为英国军事史上最惨重的灾难，随后发生了屠杀华人的“肃清”事件。

sources.title: Christopher Bayly & Tim Harper, Forgotten Armies: The Fall of British Asia, 1941–1945 (Allen Lane, 2004)
C. M. Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore 1819–2005 (NUS Press, 2009)
National Archives of Singapore / National Library Board: The Fall of Singapore
Wikipedia: Fall of Singapore

story.en:
Singapore was meant to be the impregnable "Gibraltar of the East", a naval base with heavy guns facing the sea. The Japanese came by land. Landing in southern Thailand and northern Malaya on 8 December 1941, the hour of Pearl Harbor, General Yamashita Tomoyuki's 25th Army pushed down the peninsula, using bicycles and flanking moves by sea, while Japanese bombers sank the battleships Prince of Wales and Repulse off Kuantan.

By the end of January 1942 the defenders had blown the causeway and withdrawn to the island. On the night of 8 February Japanese troops crossed the Johor Strait in the northwest. Within a week they held the reservoirs, and the crowded city faced thirst and shelling. On 15 February, the first day of the Chinese New Year, Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival signed the surrender at the Ford factory at Bukit Timah. Yamashita, who was short of ammunition, had bluffed.

Singapore became Syonan-to. In the Sook Ching ("purge through cleansing") screenings that followed, Japanese military police executed tens of thousands of Chinese men. The surrender shattered the prestige of British rule in Asia, which never fully recovered.
story.zh:
新加坡本应是固若金汤的“东方直布罗陀”，海军基地的重炮全都朝向大海。日军却从陆路而来。1941年12月8日，就在偷袭珍珠港的同一时刻，山下奉文的第二十五军在泰国南部和马来亚北部登陆，借助自行车和海上迂回沿半岛南下；日本轰炸机则在关丹外海击沉了“威尔士亲王”号和“反击”号战列舰。

到1942年1月底，守军炸断长堤，退守新加坡岛。2月8日夜，日军在西北部渡过柔佛海峡，一周之内控制了水库，拥挤的城市陷入缺水和炮击。2月15日，正是农历新年初一，白思华中将在武吉知马的福特汽车厂签署投降书。其实山下奉文的弹药已经告急，他是在虚张声势。

新加坡被改名为“昭南岛”。在随后的“大检证”（肃清）中，日本宪兵处决了数以万计的华人男子。这次投降粉碎了英国在亚洲统治的威信，从此再未完全恢复。

summary.en: After the surrender of Bataan, the Japanese forced some 60,000–80,000 Filipino and American prisoners to march about 100 km in tropical heat to San Fernando and then on to Camp O'Donnell. Thousands died of beatings, bayonetings, thirst and disease on the march and many more in the camp.
summary.zh: 巴丹守军投降后，日军强迫约六万至八万名菲律宾和美国战俘在酷热中步行约100公里到圣费尔南多，再转往奥唐奈营。数千人在行军途中死于殴打、刺刀、干渴和疾病，死于战俘营者更多。

label.zh: 邦板牙圣费尔南多（火车站）

sources.title: Michael Norman & Elizabeth M. Norman, Tears in the Darkness: The Story of the Bataan Death March (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2009)
Teodoro A. Agoncillo, History of the Filipino People (8th ed., Garotech, 1990)
Wikipedia: Bataan Death March

note: Numbers of marchers and deaths are estimates (often 5,000–18,000 Filipino and 500–650 American deaths on the march).

summary.en: To supply its army in Burma, Japan built a 415 km railway from Ban Pong in Thailand to Thanbyuzayat in Burma in about a year. Some 12,000 Allied prisoners of war and perhaps 90,000 Asian labourers, mostly from Malaya, Burma and Java, died of overwork, cholera and starvation.
summary.zh: 为补给驻缅日军，日本在约一年内修建了从泰国班蓬到缅甸丹彪扎亚、全长415公里的铁路。约一万二千名盟军战俘以及可能多达九万名主要来自马来亚、缅甸和爪哇的亚洲劳工死于过度劳累、霍乱和饥饿。

label.en: Bridge over the Khwae Yai, Kanchanaburi

sources.title: Christopher Bayly & Tim Harper, Forgotten Armies: The Fall of British Asia, 1941–1945 (Allen Lane, 2004)
Australian War Memorial: Burma–Thailand Railway
Wikipedia: Burma Railway

note: Deaths among Asian labourers (rōmusha) are poorly recorded; estimates range widely.

summary.en: France fought to reclaim Indochina from the Viet Minh, which had declared independence in 1945. A colonial reconquest became a Cold War conflict as China armed the Viet Minh and the United States paid most of France's costs, ending with defeat at Điện Biên Phủ and the Geneva partition at the 17th parallel.
summary.zh: 法国为从1945年宣布独立的越盟手中夺回印度支那而战。随着中国武装越盟、美国承担法国大部分军费，一场殖民地再征服演变为冷战冲突，最终以奠边府战败和日内瓦会议以北纬17度线分治告终。

label.en: Viet Minh win the border battle on Route 4
label.zh: 越盟赢得4号公路边界战役

label.en: French defeat at Điện Biên Phủ

sources.title: Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War: The Fall of an Empire and the Making of America's Vietnam (Random House, 2012)
Christopher Goscha, The Road to Dien Bien Phu: A History of the First War for Vietnam (Princeton University Press, 2022)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Indochina wars
Wikipedia: First Indochina War

story.en:
When Hồ Chí Minh declared independence in Hanoi in September 1945, Japanese troops still held Indochina and the French were weak. Over the next year France returned to the south and negotiated with the Viet Minh in the north, but the talks failed. In November 1946 a customs dispute at Haiphong led the French navy to shell the city, killing thousands, and on 19 December the Viet Minh attacked French positions in Hanoi and withdrew to the mountains of the Việt Bắc.

For three years it was a guerrilla war. Then Mao's victory in 1949 gave the Viet Minh a friendly border, Chinese advisers and artillery. In October 1950 Võ Nguyên Giáp destroyed the French garrisons along Route 4 near the Chinese frontier, France's worst colonial defeat since Montcalm. The United States, seeing the war as part of the struggle against communism, was soon paying most of its costs.

The French built a fortified camp at Điện Biên Phủ to lure Giáp into a set-piece battle. Instead his porters hauled guns onto the surrounding hills, and the base fell on 7 May 1954. At Geneva Vietnam was divided at the 17th parallel.
story.zh:
1945年9月胡志明在河内宣布独立时，日军仍占据印度支那，法国力量薄弱。此后一年，法国重返南方，并在北方与越盟谈判，但谈判破裂。1946年11月，海防的一场海关纠纷导致法国海军炮轰该城，造成数千人死亡；12月19日，越盟进攻河内的法军阵地，随后撤入越北山区。

最初三年是一场游击战。1949年毛泽东的胜利给越盟带来了友好的边境、中国顾问和火炮。1950年10月，武元甲在中越边境附近的4号公路沿线全歼法军守备部队，这是法国自蒙卡尔姆以来最惨重的殖民地失败。美国把这场战争视为反共斗争的一部分，很快承担了大部分军费。

法军在奠边府修筑设防营地，企图引诱武元甲打一场阵地战。武元甲却让民工把火炮拖上周围山头，1954年5月7日基地陷落。在日内瓦会议上，越南以北纬17度线为界被分割。

name.zh: 菲律宾独立（马尼拉条约）

summary.en: On 4 July 1946 the United States recognised the independent Republic of the Philippines under President Manuel Roxas, ending nearly fifty years of American rule. Trade and military-base agreements kept close ties; in 1962 the Philippines moved Independence Day to 12 June.
summary.zh: 1946年7月4日，美国承认以罗哈斯为总统的菲律宾共和国独立，结束了近五十年的美国统治。贸易和军事基地协定维持了两国的紧密关系；1962年菲律宾把独立日改为6月12日。

sources.title: Teodoro A. Agoncillo, History of the Filipino People (8th ed., Garotech, 1990)
US Department of State, Office of the Historian: Philippine Independence
Wikipedia: Treaty of Manila (1946)

summary.en: At 4:20 in the morning, an hour chosen by astrologers, the Union of Burma became independent outside the Commonwealth. Its architect Aung San had been assassinated six months earlier; within three months the communists, and within a year the Karen, took up arms, beginning civil wars that still divide the country.
summary.zh: 凌晨4时20分，这一由占星师选定的时刻，缅甸联邦宣告独立，且不加入英联邦。独立的缔造者昂山已于六个月前遇刺；三个月内缅甸共产党、一年之内克伦族武装相继起事，开启了至今仍撕裂这个国家的内战。

sources.title: Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
Martin Smith, Burma: Insurgency and the Politics of Ethnicity (Zed Books, 1991)
Wikipedia: Burmese Declaration of Independence

story.en:
Burma's independence was negotiated by Aung San, but he did not live to see it. After his assassination on 19 July 1947 the British turned to his colleague U Nu, who signed the transfer treaty with Attlee in October. Burma chose to leave the Commonwealth altogether, the first former colony to do so.

On 4 January 1948, at 4:20 a.m., an hour fixed by court astrologers as auspicious, the Union Jack came down in Rangoon and the new flag of the Union of Burma went up. Sao Shwe Thaik, a Shan prince, became the first president and U Nu prime minister.

The celebrations were brief. In March the Communist Party of Burma went underground and took up arms; by early 1949 Karen forces were fighting on the outskirts of Rangoon, and the government at times controlled little beyond the capital. The army that saved it, under General Ne Win, would seize power in 1962. The promises of Panglong to the frontier peoples were never fully honoured, and some of the insurgencies that began in 1948 are still fighting today.
story.zh:
缅甸的独立是由昂山谈判争取的，但他没能活着看到这一天。1947年7月19日昂山遇刺后，英国转而与他的同僚吴努打交道，双方于10月签署移交条约。缅甸选择完全退出英联邦，是第一个这样做的前殖民地。

1948年1月4日凌晨4时20分，这一由宫廷占星师择定的吉时，英国国旗在仰光降下，缅甸联邦的新国旗升起。掸族土司苏瑞泰出任首任总统，吴努出任总理。

庆祝转瞬即逝。3月，缅甸共产党转入地下并拿起武器；到1949年初，克伦武装已在仰光郊外作战，政府一度只控制首都周边。挽救政府的军队由奈温将军指挥，他后来在1962年夺取了政权。彬龙会议对边疆民族的承诺从未完全兑现，始于1948年的一些武装冲突至今仍在继续。

summary.en: After communist guerrillas killed three European planters at Sungai Siput, Britain declared an emergency against the Malayan Communist Party's mainly Chinese army. The Briggs Plan resettled over 500,000 rural Chinese into guarded "New Villages"; the insurgency faded and the emergency ended in 1960.
summary.zh: 共产党游击队在和丰杀死三名欧洲种植园主后，英国针对以华人为主的马来亚共产党武装宣布紧急状态。“布里格斯计划”把五十多万农村华人迁入有守卫的“新村”；游击战逐渐平息，紧急状态于1960年结束。

sources.title: Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Karl Hack, The Malayan Emergency: Revolution and Counterinsurgency at the End of Empire (Cambridge University Press, 2021)
Wikipedia: Malayan Emergency

note: Point at Sungai Siput, Perak, where the emergency began; the polity tag stands for British Malaya.

summary.en: Delegates of 29 Asian and African countries, most newly independent, met in Bandung at Sukarno's invitation, among them Nehru, Zhou Enlai and Nasser. Their ten principles against colonialism and for peaceful coexistence laid the groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement.
summary.zh: 应苏加诺之邀，29个亚非国家（多数刚刚独立）的代表在万隆聚会，其中有尼赫鲁、周恩来和纳赛尔。会议通过反对殖民主义、主张和平共处的十项原则，为不结盟运动奠定了基础。

sources.title: Office of the Historian, US Department of State: Bandung Conference (Asian-African Conference), 1955
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Richard Wright, The Color Curtain (World Publishing, 1956)
Wikipedia: Asian–African Conference

story.en:
In April 1955 the hill town of Bandung, once a Dutch colonial resort, hosted the first great gathering of the formerly colonised world. Delegations from 29 countries, representing more than half of humanity, met in the Gedung Merdeka, the old Dutch club. Sukarno opened the conference by calling it the first intercontinental meeting of coloured peoples in history.

The guest list spanned the Cold War divide: India's Nehru, China's Zhou Enlai, Egypt's Nasser, Kojo Botsio for the still-colonial Gold Coast and pro-Western leaders from Pakistan, Turkey and the Philippines. Zhou won admirers by soothing fears of Chinese subversion and offering to negotiate with the United States over Taiwan. The American writer Richard Wright, who attended, described the meeting as a revolt of the dispossessed against the racial order.

The final communiqué set out ten principles, among them respect for sovereignty, non-interference and the peaceful settlement of disputes. Bandung did not create a bloc, but its spirit led to the Non-Aligned Movement founded in Belgrade in 1961, and it remains a symbol of the Global South.
story.zh:
1955年4月，曾是荷兰殖民避暑胜地的山城万隆，迎来了前殖民地世界的第一次盛会。代表全人类一半以上人口的29国代表团，在原荷兰俱乐部“独立大厦”集会。苏加诺在开幕词中称之为历史上第一次有色人种的洲际会议。

与会者横跨冷战两大阵营：印度的尼赫鲁、中国的周恩来、埃及的纳赛尔、代表尚为殖民地的黄金海岸的科乔·博奇奥，以及来自巴基斯坦、土耳其和菲律宾的亲西方领导人。周恩来以消除对中国输出革命的疑虑、表示愿就台湾问题与美国谈判，赢得了许多人的好感。到场的美国作家理查德·赖特把这次会议描述为被剥夺者对种族秩序的反抗。

会议公报提出了尊重主权、互不干涉内政、和平解决争端等十项原则。万隆会议并未形成一个集团，但其精神催生了1961年在贝尔格莱德成立的不结盟运动，至今仍是“全球南方”的象征。

summary.en: In the newly built Merdeka Stadium in Kuala Lumpur, Tunku Abdul Rahman read the proclamation of independence of the Federation of Malaya and led the crowd in seven cries of "Merdeka!" ("freedom"). The Alliance of Malay, Chinese and Indian parties formed the government.
summary.zh: 在吉隆坡新建的独立体育场，东姑阿都拉曼宣读马来亚联合邦独立宣言，并带领群众七次高呼“默迪卡！”（独立）。由马来人、华人和印度人政党组成的联盟党组建了政府。

sources.title: Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
National Archives of Malaysia: Proclamation of Independence 1957
Wikipedia: Malayan Declaration of Independence

summary.en: Malaya, Singapore, Sarawak and North Borneo (Sabah) joined to form Malaysia; Brunei stayed out. Indonesia under Sukarno answered with Konfrontasi, an undeclared border war in Borneo, and the Philippines pressed its claim to Sabah.
summary.zh: 马来亚、新加坡、砂拉越和北婆罗洲（沙巴）合组马来西亚，文莱未加入。苏加诺领导的印尼以“对抗”政策回应，在婆罗洲发动不宣而战的边境战争；菲律宾则坚持对沙巴的主权要求。

sources.title: Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
C. M. Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore 1819–2005 (NUS Press, 2009)
Wikipedia: Proclamation of Malaysia

name.zh: 新加坡脱离马来西亚独立

summary.en: After two years of conflict between the PAP and UMNO over Malay privileges, and race riots in 1964, Tunku Abdul Rahman had Singapore expelled from Malaysia. Lee Kuan Yew wept on television as he announced the independence he had not wanted.
summary.zh: 人民行动党与巫统围绕马来人特权争执两年，1964年又发生种族骚乱，东姑阿都拉曼最终将新加坡逐出马来西亚。李光耀在电视上宣布这一他并不想要的独立时潸然泪下。

sources.title: C. M. Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore 1819–2005 (NUS Press, 2009)
Lee Kuan Yew, The Singapore Story (Times Editions, 1998)
Wikipedia: Independence of Singapore Agreement 1965

note: The agreement was signed on 7 August and took effect on 9 August 1965.

summary.en: After the still-debated 30 September Movement killed six army generals, the army under Suharto blamed the Communist Party (PKI) and, with militias, killed perhaps 500,000 or more alleged communists, many of them in Java and Bali; hundreds of thousands were imprisoned. The killings opened Suharto's 32-year New Order.
summary.zh: 扑朔迷离的“九三〇运动”杀害六名陆军将领后，苏哈托领导的军队归罪于印尼共产党，并与民兵一道杀害了约五十万甚至更多被指为共产党人的民众，其中许多在爪哇和巴厘；数十万人遭监禁。这场屠杀开启了苏哈托长达32年的“新秩序”统治。

sources.title: Geoffrey B. Robinson, The Killing Season: A History of the Indonesian Massacres, 1965–66 (Princeton University Press, 2018)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
John Roosa, Pretext for Mass Murder (University of Wisconsin Press, 2006)
Wikipedia: Indonesian mass killings of 1965–66

note: Death toll estimates range from about 500,000 to over one million. Point placed in Central Java, one of the worst-affected regions.

story.en:
In the early hours of 1 October 1965, troops of a group calling itself the 30 September Movement kidnapped and killed six senior army generals in Jakarta and announced that they had forestalled a coup. Major General Suharto, commander of the army's strategic reserve, crushed the movement within a day and declared it the work of the Indonesian Communist Party (PKI), then the largest communist party outside the communist bloc.

What followed was one of the largest mass killings of the 20th century. From late October army units, especially paratroopers under Sarwo Edhie, moved through Central Java, East Java and later Bali, arming and directing Muslim youth groups, nationalist militias and local gangs. Suspected communists, members of peasant and women's organisations, and in places ethnic Chinese were rounded up and killed, often at night by rivers. Rivers in East Java were said to be choked with bodies. Declassified records studied by historians such as Geoffrey Robinson show that the United States and Britain knew of the killings and gave the army support.

Sukarno was sidelined and Suharto became president in 1967–68. For three decades the killings were celebrated as the nation's salvation, and survivors and their families lived with stigma. Only after 1998 did Indonesians begin to speak about them openly.
story.zh:
1965年10月1日凌晨，一支自称“九三〇运动”的部队在雅加达绑架并杀害了六名陆军高级将领，宣称他们挫败了一场政变。陆军战略后备部队司令苏哈托少将在一天之内粉碎了这一运动，并宣布它是印尼共产党所为——当时印共是社会主义阵营之外最大的共产党。

随之而来的是20世纪规模最大的屠杀之一。从10月下旬起，军队（尤其是萨尔沃·埃迪指挥的伞兵）先后进入中爪哇、东爪哇，后来又到巴厘岛，武装并指挥穆斯林青年团体、民族主义民兵和地方帮派。被怀疑的共产党人、农民和妇女组织成员，以及一些地方的华人，被围捕杀害，往往是在夜里的河边。据说东爪哇的河流被尸体堵塞。杰弗里·罗宾逊等历史学家依据解密档案指出，美国和英国知悉这场屠杀，并向军方提供了支持。

苏加诺被架空，苏哈托于1967—1968年成为总统。三十年间，这场屠杀被歌颂为拯救国家之举，幸存者及其家属背负着污名生活。直到1998年以后，印尼人才开始公开谈论这段历史。

name.en: Laotian Civil War and the "Secret War"

summary.en: The royal government, backed by the CIA and Hmong forces under Vang Pao, fought the communist Pathet Lao, backed by North Vietnam. American aircraft flew some 580,000 bombing missions over Laos from 1964 to 1973, making it the most heavily bombed country per head in history. The Pathet Lao took power in 1975.
summary.zh: 得到美国中央情报局和王宝领导的苗族武装支持的王国政府，与北越支持的共产党巴特寮作战。1964年至1973年间，美国飞机在老挝执行了约58万架次轰炸任务，使其成为历史上人均遭轰炸最严重的国家。1975年巴特寮掌权。

sources.title: Martin Stuart-Fox, A History of Laos (Cambridge University Press, 1997)
Joshua Kurlantzick, A Great Place to Have a War (Simon & Schuster, 2017)
Wikipedia: Laotian Civil War

note: Point at the Plain of Jars, the main battleground.

name.zh: 越南入侵柬埔寨（柬越战争）

summary.en: After repeated Khmer Rouge massacres in its border provinces, Vietnam invaded on 25 December 1978 and took Phnom Penh on 7 January 1979, ending Democratic Kampuchea. China retaliated with a border war in February 1979; Vietnamese troops stayed in Cambodia, fighting Khmer Rouge guerrillas, until 1989.
summary.zh: 红色高棉多次在越南边境省份屠杀平民后，越南于1978年12月25日出兵，1979年1月7日攻占金边，终结了民主柬埔寨。中国于1979年2月发动边境战争予以报复；越军留驻柬埔寨与红色高棉游击队作战，直到1989年撤出。

sources.title: Ben Kiernan, The Pol Pot Regime (Yale University Press, 3rd ed. 2008)
Nayan Chanda, Brother Enemy: The War after the War (Harcourt Brace Jovanovich, 1986)
Wikipedia: Cambodian–Vietnamese War

note: Border clashes began in 1977 (Wikidata's start); the full invasion was in December 1978.

summary.en: After 1975, and especially in 1978–79 when Hanoi pressed many ethnic Chinese to leave, hundreds of thousands fled Vietnam in small boats. How many died at sea from storms, hunger and pirates is unknown; estimates run as high as 200,000–400,000. Camps such as Pulau Bidong in Malaysia sheltered survivors until resettlement abroad.
summary.zh: 1975年后，尤其是1978—1979年河内迫使大批华人离境期间，数十万人乘小船逃离越南。死于海上风暴、饥饿和海盗的人数无从确知，估计最高达二十万至四十万。马来西亚比东岛等难民营收容幸存者，直到他们被安置到海外。

sources.title: UNHCR, The State of the World's Refugees 2000, ch. 4: Flight from Indochina
W. Courtland Robinson, Terms of Refuge: The Indochinese Exodus and the International Response (Zed Books, 1998)
Wikipedia: Vietnamese boat people

note: Death estimates are uncertain and vary widely. Point at Pulau Bidong, the largest first-asylum camp.

summary.en: Facing hyperinflation and hunger, the Sixth Congress of the Vietnamese Communist Party under Nguyễn Văn Linh launched "renovation": household farming, private enterprise and foreign investment within a one-party state. Within a few years Vietnam went from importing rice to being one of the world's largest rice exporters.
summary.zh: 面对恶性通胀与饥荒，越南共产党在阮文灵领导下召开第六次代表大会，推行“革新”：在一党体制下实行家庭承包、允许私营经济和引进外资。几年之内，越南由大米进口国变为世界主要的大米出口国之一。

sources.title: Adam Fforde & Stefan de Vylder, From Plan to Market: The Economic Transition in Vietnam (Westview, 1996)
World Bank: Vietnam Overview
Wikipedia: Đổi Mới

summary.en: Students, monks and workers rose against General Ne Win's one-party rule in nationwide protests that peaked on 8 August 1988. Aung San Suu Kyi addressed half a million people at the Shwedagon Pagoda; the army crushed the movement in a coup on 18 September and installed the SLORC junta; perhaps 3,000 people were killed in all.
summary.zh: 学生、僧侣和工人发起全国性抗议，反对奈温将军的一党统治，于1988年8月8日达到高潮。昂山素季在瑞光大金塔向五十万民众发表演说；9月18日军队发动政变镇压运动，成立“国家恢复法律与秩序委员会”军政府；前后约三千人遇难。

sources.title: Bertil Lintner, Outrage: Burma's Struggle for Democracy (White Lotus, 1990)
Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
Wikipedia: 8888 Uprising

note: Casualty figures are estimates.

summary.en: When Thailand floated the baht on 2 July 1997, it collapsed, and capital fled from Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and South Korea. The rupiah lost over 80 per cent of its value; IMF rescue programmes imposed austerity, and the crisis brought down Suharto.
summary.zh: 1997年7月2日泰国放弃泰铢固定汇率后，泰铢暴跌，资本随即逃离印尼、马来西亚、菲律宾和韩国。印尼盾贬值逾八成；国际货币基金组织的救援计划附带紧缩条件，这场危机最终使苏哈托下台。

sources.title: International Monetary Fund: Recovery from the Asian Crisis and the Role of the IMF (2000)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Wikipedia: 1997 Asian financial crisis

name.zh: 苏哈托下台与“改革运动”

summary.en: With the economy in ruins, the shooting of four students at Trisakti University on 12 May 1998 sparked riots in Jakarta in which over a thousand died and Chinese Indonesians were targeted. Students occupied parliament, and on 21 May Suharto resigned after 32 years, opening the era of Reformasi.
summary.zh: 经济崩溃之际，1998年5月12日特里萨克蒂大学四名学生遭枪杀，引发雅加达骚乱，一千多人丧生，华裔印尼人成为攻击目标。学生占领国会，5月21日执政32年的苏哈托辞职，“改革”时代由此开启。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Edward Aspinall, Opposing Suharto: Compromise, Resistance, and Regime Change in Indonesia (Stanford University Press, 2005)
Wikipedia: Fall of Suharto

summary.en: In a UN-run referendum 78.5 per cent of East Timorese rejected autonomy within Indonesia. Army-backed militias then killed some 1,400 people and burned much of the territory until an Australian-led force (INTERFET) arrived; after UN administration Timor-Leste became independent on 20 May 2002.
summary.zh: 在联合国主持的公投中，78.5%的东帝汶人拒绝留在印尼享有自治。随后军方支持的民兵杀害约1400人，焚毁了大片地区，直到澳大利亚领导的国际部队抵达；经过联合国过渡管理，东帝汶于2002年5月20日独立。

sources.title: Geoffrey Robinson, "If You Leave Us Here, We Will Die": How Genocide Was Stopped in East Timor (Princeton University Press, 2010)
United Nations: UNTAET mission background
Wikipedia: 1999 East Timorese independence referendum

summary.en: A cyclone drove a storm surge of several metres across the low Irrawaddy delta, leaving about 138,000 people dead or missing. The military junta at first blocked foreign aid workers and went ahead with a constitutional referendum a week later.
summary.zh: 一场强气旋风暴把数米高的风暴潮推过低洼的伊洛瓦底江三角洲，造成约13.8万人死亡或失踪。军政府起初阻止外国救援人员入境，并在一周后照常举行宪法公投。

sources.title: Tripartite Core Group (ASEAN, UN, Myanmar), Post-Nargis Joint Assessment (2008)
Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
Wikipedia: Cyclone Nargis

note: Point at Labutta, one of the worst-hit towns. The 138,000 figure (dead and missing) is the joint government–ASEAN–UN assessment; the junta's early counts were far lower.

summary.en: One of the strongest tropical cyclones ever to make landfall struck the central Philippines; its storm surge flattened much of Tacloban. More than 6,300 people died and some four million were displaced.
summary.zh: 有记录以来登陆时强度最大的热带气旋之一袭击菲律宾中部，风暴潮几乎夷平了塔克洛班。6300多人死亡，约四百万人流离失所。

sources.title: NDRRMC (Philippines), Final Report on Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) (2014)
NASA Earth Observatory: Super Typhoon Haiyan
Wikipedia: Typhoon Haiyan

summary.en: After militant attacks on border posts, Myanmar's army carried out "clearance operations" in northern Rakhine in 2016 and especially from August 2017, burning hundreds of villages; more than 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh. A UN fact-finding mission called for generals to be tried for genocide, and The Gambia brought a case at the International Court of Justice.
summary.zh: 武装分子袭击边境哨所后，缅甸军队于2016年、尤其是2017年8月起在若开邦北部实施“清剿行动”，焚毁数百个村庄，七十多万罗兴亚人逃往孟加拉国。联合国实况调查团呼吁以种族灭绝罪审判相关将领，冈比亚向国际法院提起诉讼。

sources.title: UN Human Rights Council, Report of the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar (A/HRC/39/64, 2018)
International Court of Justice: The Gambia v. Myanmar
Wikipedia: Rohingya genocide

note: Point at Maungdaw, northern Rakhine; Wikidata's point is central Myanmar.

summary.en: On the morning the new parliament was due to sit, the army under Min Aung Hlaing detained Aung San Suu Kyi and her government, alleging election fraud. Mass protests and a civil disobedience movement were met with lethal force, and the resistance turned into a nationwide armed conflict.
summary.zh: 在新一届议会预定开会的当天早晨，敏昂莱领导的军队以选举舞弊为由拘押了昂山素季及其政府成员。大规模抗议和公民不服从运动遭到致命武力镇压，抵抗随之演变为全国性的武装冲突。

sources.title: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights: Myanmar reports (2021–2024)
Thant Myint-U, The Hidden History of Burma (W. W. Norton, 2019)
Wikipedia: 2021 Myanmar coup d'état

name.zh: 特尔纳特驱逐葡萄牙人

summary.en: After the Portuguese had Sultan Hairun murdered inside their fort on Ternate in 1570, his son Baabullah rallied the clove islands and besieged the fortress of São João Baptista for five years. In 1575 the starving garrison surrendered and withdrew, and Ternate under Baabullah became the leading power of eastern Indonesia.
summary.zh: 1570年葡萄牙人在特尔纳特的要塞内谋杀了苏丹海伦，其子巴布拉联合丁香群岛各方，围攻圣若昂·巴蒂斯塔要塞长达五年。1575年饥困的守军投降撤离，特尔纳特在巴布拉治下成为印尼东部的头号强国。
